docs.text: ru-misra : MISRA C++:2023 analysis with the CodeQL coding-standards pack (2.62.0, CLI 2.21.4) and the Kokeb C++20 profile pack on traced host and Cortex-M builds, the handbook's deviation records applied through the pack's deviation mechanism (a marker must cite a record and deviate a finding of its guideline), clang-tidy's validated checks and cppcheck on the same compile databases, and a per-guideline report (step summary, SARIF, JSON keyed by guideline, CSV). Levels high and safety . Every scan analyses a canary and fails on incomplete extraction. The first job refuses private repositories without an Advanced Security licence (CodeQL terms). Needs contents: read . Tool validation of the MISRA toolchain ( docs/tool-validation/plan.md ): requirements derived from the compliance matrix and the pack, a seeded-violation and compliant case per requirement ( tests/misra-validation/ ), a traceability page, an anomaly log, and a validation report attached to each release. The self-CI fails when a tool-decided guideline has no passing test, or when the toolchain changes without re-validation. codeql/kokeb-cpp20 : the own C++20 profile query pack, with KB-CPP-046 (Result types are [[nodiscard]] ). ru-misra : open_source_prerelease lets a private repository whose code is under the OSI licence in its LICENSE file, and is to be published, run the analysis; the job prints the declaration as a warning. Code scanning of ci-tools moves to an advanced setup ( .github/workflows/codeql.yml , security-and-quality ) that leaves out the test fixtures, which break rules on purpose and whose findings the self-CI asserts. ru-misra passes cmake_args and paths to its scanner as --option=value , so a value that starts with -D is not read as an option; the fixture self-test now passes one. ru-misra gives CodeQL an explicit heap (the runner's memory less 2 GiB); the analysis ran out of memory on the 2-core runners of private repositories. A tool suppression must cite a deviation record only when it can silence a finding the matrix relies on (a cppcheck suppression, a bare NOLINT , or one naming a validated clang-tidy check); NOLINTEND never needs one. A validated clang-tidy claim can carry message: , a regex the diagnostic must match to count: a check that reports more than its guideline (cppcoreguidelines-macro-usage and object-like macros) decides only that part. ru-misra 's extraction check skips a unit the build defines but never compiles (no object file: a target outside all , such as a compile-fail test, or one the Cortex-M target does not build) and lists it as not analysed. ru-misra reads the tool validation's anomaly log: at the high level, findings of a rule with a recorded false positive are listed for review (with the anomaly ids) instead of failing the job; validated rules still fail. Tool validation: every seeded violation is marked ( // seeded ) and every claimed tool must report on that line, so a bad file that seeds several forms proves each detection; an independent review of all cases against the guidelines corrected the cases that tested the wrong thing and added the missing forms. New cases record the misreadings of class-template code found by the first driver scans. The CodeQL databases are traced with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , as the scans build; clang-tidy claims accept known_misses .
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-build : the native build no longer downloads ccache on every run. The pinned, hash-checked binary is kept in the Actions cache by version; a download retries on every error with a delay, and one that still fails falls back to the runner's ccache package with a warning. GitHub release downloads returning HTTP 504 had failed whole ESP32 jobs. Self-CI caches its pinned shellcheck and actionlint by version and hash and retries their download on any error; ru-cross-build and ru-docs-publish retry their release downloads on any error (HTTP 5xx included). ru-docs-linkcheck and ru-mkdocs-publish run lychee 0.24.2 installed by the job (pinned, SHA-256-checked, kept in the Actions cache) instead of lycheeverse/lychee-action , which downloaded it from GitHub releases on every run. Same arguments, same failure rule; the link report goes to the step summary. ru-docs-publish (legacy): Doxygen 1.10.0 is kept in the Actions cache by version (falling back to the runner's package with a warning when GitHub releases fail), and its link check runs the same cached lychee.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-build : input idf_install (default native ). The job installs ESP-IDF for the matrix target only (a shallow clone and install.sh <target> , about 1.1 GB) and keeps it in the Actions cache keyed by the commit the IDF version names, with a pinned, hash-checked ccache. A warm restore takes about 20 s, against 70 to 160 s to pull the 9.4 GB espressif/idf image; a Debug and Release build of one app dropped from 175 s to 93 s. idf_install: docker keeps the image and espressif/esp-idf-ci-action .
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-repo-checks : DCO, the organisation standard, Markdown lint, the handbook rules, template drift, cppcheck and YAML lint as steps of one job, with the same scripts, pinned actions, failure rules and summaries as dco , org-standard-check , ru-markdown-lint , ru-handbook-check , ru-template-drift , ru-cpp-analysis and ru-yaml-lint . DCO runs first, before any checkout, and passes with nothing to check outside a pull request, so the gate needs no allow_skipped for it. Needs contents: read and pull-requests: read . The self-CI ( check_repo_checks.py ) fails when a copied step differs from its single workflow. The single workflows stay. ru-cross-build : input per_core_jobs (default false ) keeps one job per core. ru-host-quality : input separate_jobs (default false ) keeps one job per check. Trigger policy ( docs/triggers.md ), enforced by the self-CI ( check_triggers.py ): workflows start only from push , pull_request , merge_group and workflow_call , with release.yml 's workflow_run as the one exception.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: The self-test callers ( ci-*.yml ) and the mkdocs-site template no longer have a workflow_dispatch trigger: a manual run is a re-run. A dispatched run executes in the default branch's context and can write the cache that runs on main restore, which made every checkout of a pinned ci-tools or driver-template commit a CodeQL actions/cache-poisoning/poisonable-step finding. The examples in the docs drop it too. ru-cross-build : every core is built in one job, one after the other, each in its own build directory and log group; a core that fails does not stop the others. The toolchain is downloaded once, and a private repository is billed one rounded-up job instead of four (the plan job and one per core). ru-host-quality : complexity, coverage and sanitizers run as steps of one job, each still running when another failed, with the same limits, summaries, artifacts and outputs; the limits job is gone (each job resolves the limits itself). Fuzzing stays a job of its own and no longer waits for the limits job. A private repository is billed one rounded-up job instead of four.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: ru-build : input group_build_types (default true ) builds every build type of an app and IDF version in one job, so the runner is prepared and the ESP-IDF image pulled once per app instead of once per build type. The job name and artifact name list the build types together ( Debug Release ).
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-build : ccache's directory is now kept between runs ( actions/cache , skipped with clean_build ). Before, IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE left it inside the container and every build started cold. ru-build : the runner's unused SDKs are removed in parallel, and only when less than 30 GB is free. ru-mkdocs-publish : the Lighthouse and screenshots job caches pip's wheels, the @lhci/cli download and Playwright's Chromium.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: ru-template-drift : with enforce: false the job failed instead of warning when the scaffold printed only to stderr (an empty report made the summary's grep fail). The scaffold's errors now reach the log and the summary.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-template-drift : compares the files driver-template manages (workflows, _config/ , skills, CMake helpers) with what the template makes today from the caller's .kokeb/template.yml , using the template's own scaffold.py --check-drift . It warns by default; enforce: true fails on drift. The signed-release job had already drifted: two drivers had it and the template did not.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-mkdocs-publish : a pre-release tag ( vX.Y.Z-rc.N ) no longer takes the latest alias, and with release_version: minor no longer overwrites the docs of its minor; it publishes under its own tag. The first release candidate of driver-pcal9555 moved latest off dev , against the release standard.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-attest-release : signed build provenance (GitHub artifact attestation, SLSA, Sigstore) for every file of a published release, after the files are checked against its SHA256SUMS . Callers add it as a job after ru-release or ru-release-with-artifacts and grant id-token: write and attestations: write . Public repositories, or GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-release and ru-release-with-artifacts attach supply-chain files to every release: a source archive with a stable checksum ( <name>-<version>.tar.gz ), an SPDX 2.3 SBOM ( <name>-<version>.spdx.json : the repository, its licence and tagged commit, each git submodule at its pinned commit, each firmware zip) and SHA256SUMS . Built by the new tools/release_assets/release_assets.py (standard library only, unit-tested in the self-CI); the checksums also go to the run summary. Signed provenance waits for public repositories ( docs/ru-release-with-artifacts.md#provenance ).
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-release-with-artifacts attaches one zip per firmware artifact, holding what flashes and debugs each ESP-IDF build ( flasher_args.json , flash_args , the files they flash, the app .elf and .map ), instead of every file of the build folders. The old upload sent about 2,900 files for a driver with a Debug and a Release build, past GitHub's limit of 1,000 per release, and files of the same name in Debug and Release overwrote each other.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: ru-host-quality : a fuzz job. With fuzz_cmake_args set (for example -DMYCHIP_BUILD_FUZZERS=ON ), it builds with clang 18 and libFuzzer, ASan and UBSan, and fuzzes every fuzz_<name> executable for fuzz_seconds (by level: 60, 120, 600 s). Each target starts from its committed seeds in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_<name>/ plus a corpus cached between runs. The step summary has runs, coverage edges and corpus size per target, and a failing input is uploaded as <artifact_name>-fuzz-crashes . Without fuzz_cmake_args nothing changes.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-handbook-check : the rules snapshot follows the handbook's ADR-0021 ( EnsureInitialized() is the one start-up entry point: KB-CPP-043, KB-CPP-058, KB-CPP-059) and the new datasheet-trail rule KB-DOC-065.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: ru-host-quality : coverage merges the instances of a template ( gcovr --merge-lines ), so a line, branch or condition counts as covered when any instance ran it. A header-only driver is compiled once per port type, and an example's instance that runs only the happy path counted every failure path again, as uncovered: the AS5047U driver measured 73.8 % of branches instead of 94.5 %.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-host-quality : the complexity job now measures header-only implementation files ( .ipp , .tpp , .inl ). lizard picks the files of a directory by extension and skipped them, so a driver whose code lives in src/<chip>.ipp had its implementation unmeasured. The job lists every C and C++ file under library_paths itself; the self-test fixture has a too-complex function in an .ipp file as well and must report both. ru-cpp-lint : extensions defaults to c,cpp,cc,cxx,h,hpp,ipp,tpp,inl , so clang-format checks header-only implementation files. clang-tidy skips those files as translation units and reports on them through the sources that include them, as before. Callers that set extensions add ipp themselves.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-handbook-check : checks a repository against the Kokeb Labs handbook rules a script can decide. It reads the .kokeb/handbook.yml declaration (handbook version, kind, assurance level, waivers) and checks the root layout, driver.yml against the build settings, C++20 and no file(GLOB) in CMake, no heap, exceptions, RTTI or virtual functions in driver code, the target library subset of headers, and no committed sdkconfig or datasheet. Each finding names its rule, quotes its title and links to it; a rule still in its warning period warns, a waived rule is a notice, and an expired waiver fails. The checker ( tools/handbook_check/ ) and its snapshot of the rules are fetched at this workflow's own commit; 15 unit tests and good and bad fixture repositories run under the CI gate.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: tools/docs-migrate.py : a character range listed twice in the emoji pattern (CodeQL py/overly-large-range ).
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-cross-build : builds one CMake target for Cortex-M0+, M3, M4F, M7F and M33F cores with Arm's GNU toolchain 14.3.rel1 (pinned, SHA-256 checked; an Ubuntu mirror hung one install for 20 minutes), one job per core, with the caller's own warning and language flags, and reports the objects' code and data size. A driver proves its code compiles for a microcontroller, not only on the host.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-release-with-artifacts takes a commit input: the commit whose CI artifacts are released, for callers that release from a finished CI run ( workflow_run ), where github.sha is the default branch's head. It also checks that the release tag points to that commit before releasing. The guide shows a caller that releases only after CI passed on the tag.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: ru-build no longer fails pull requests from forks: their token cannot comment, so the size comment is skipped for them (and never fails the job), and the size table is always written to the run summary. On same-repository pull requests the comment is updated on each push instead of added again.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: ru-yaml-lint installs yamllint 1.38.0 pinned with SHA-256 hashes on ubuntu-24.04 , instead of the latest yamllint from an unpinned pip install . ru-host-ci passes artifact_name through the environment instead of expanding it inside a shell command. ru-markdown-lint with use_docker: true pulled markdownlint/markdownlint-cli2:latest , an image that does not exist; it now uses the author's image davidanson/markdownlint-cli2 , pinned to v0.23.3 by digest.
docs.title: Security

docs.text: ru-cpp-lint runs clang-format 20.1.8 and clang-tidy 20.1.0 itself, from LLVM's builds on PyPI pinned with their SHA-256, instead of cpp-linter-action. That action installed clang from LLVM's apt server, fetching and running its install script as root without a pinned version or checksum, and the install hung for 20 minutes several times a day. The job now needs only contents: read ; thread_comments and lines_changed_only are accepted but ignored (whole files are checked). Findings are annotations and a run-summary table, as before.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: The cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action and hustcer/setup-nu actions are no longer used, so they can leave the organisation's allow-list.
docs.title: Security

docs.text: ru-host-quality : complexity (lizard, modified cyclomatic complexity, length, parameters), coverage (GCC 14 and gcovr: lines, branches and MC/DC from -fcondition-coverage ) and AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer jobs, with the limits the Kokeb Labs handbook sets per assurance level ( level: standard | high | safety ). Tools are pinned and hash-checked. Its self-test runs under the CI gate, including a fixture over every complexity limit that must be reported.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: A release waits for the whole self-CI on the merged commit ( release.yml runs on workflow_run of "🧪 Workflow Self-CI"). The self-tests of the reusable workflows ( ci-*.yml ) are now called from ci-self.yml , so the required "CI gate" covers them: a red reusable workflow can neither merge nor reach @v1 . The Markdown lint self-test reports issues instead of fixing them in the runner. ru-cpp-lint fails the job when clang-format or clang-tidy reports a finding ( fail_on_findings , default true); before, findings were only annotated and the job always passed. A new cmake_args input configures CMake with compile_commands.json , so clang-tidy sees the project's include paths; without it clang-tidy could not find the project's own headers. A findings output gives the count. ru-cpp-analysis runs cppcheck from Ubuntu's archive instead of the unpinned ghcr.io/facthunder/cppcheck:latest image, no longer ignores cppcheck's own exit status, counts findings from the XML report ( strict used to fail on every run, because the report always has a header), defaults std to c++20 , takes an artifact_name , and has a findings output. Releases of this repository are cut from CHANGELOG.md : a pull request that should be released moves the Unreleased entries to a new ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section ( python .github/scripts/changelog.py bump patch ), and merging it tags that version, publishes the section as the release notes and moves v1 . Before, every merge was tagged and the changelog was left behind. The self-CI checks that a new section is the next version, is dated, and is a major when it has ### Breaking .
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: The bundled fonts' @font-face rules moved from kokeb.css to assets/kokeb/fonts.css , which loads without blocking the first paint (as Google Fonts did before). Referenced from the render-blocking stylesheet, the font files sat on Lighthouse's critical path and the portal's performance score fell from about 0.89 to 0.78.
docs.title: Fixed

docs.text: Bundled fonts used font-display: optional without a preload. This did not restore the Lighthouse score and was replaced in 1.0.5.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: The kokeb docs theme ships Inter and JetBrains Mono itself (variable woff2, SIL Open Font License) instead of loading them from Google Fonts, so no Kokeb page sends a reader's address to Google. ru-mkdocs-publish copies the fonts beside the Doxygen stylesheet for the API pages; the root 404 page uses system fonts.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: Mermaid, still loaded on demand from unpkg, is pinned to 11.17.2 and checked with Subresource Integrity, so a changed file on the CDN is refused instead of run.
docs.title: Security

docs.text: ru-docs-publish installs Doxygen from its own release, checked against a pinned SHA-256, and Graphviz with apt, instead of two small third-party actions ( ssciwr/doxygen-install , tlylt/install-graphviz ).
docs.title: Security

docs.text: figkit draws in the Kokeb palette (copper on light, star gold on dark), and its legend can explain solid and dashed arrows. A region can put its caption on a second line. The workflow figure shows the push lane and the tag lane apart, with labelled arrows. The style guide says how a figure reads: one direction, a verb on every arrow, colour for ownership.
docs.title: Changed

docs.text: First release of kokeb-labs/ci-tools .

Reusable workflows for C/C++ ( ru-host-ci , ru-cpp-lint , ru-cpp-analysis ), documentation ( ru-mkdocs-publish , ru-docs-publish , ru-docs-linkcheck ), Markdown and YAML lint ( ru-markdown-lint , ru-yaml-lint ), releases ( ru-release ) and the single required check ( ru-ci-gate ). ESP-IDF firmware workflows in the same repository: ru-build (matrix build from app_config.yml , size report and budget) and ru-release-with-artifacts (release with the tested firmware), plus the ensure-tools-directory composite action. The build finds or clones espidf-tools . dco.yml : fails a pull request when a commit lacks a Signed-off-by: line matching its author. org-standard-check.yml : fails when README.md , LICENSE , CHANGELOG.md or .github/CODEOWNERS is missing, or when LICENSE is not the MIT licence. packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme : the documentation theme ( theme: kokeb ), plugin ( plugins: [kokeb] ), figkit and the kokeb-docs command, with the pinned MkDocs toolchain. The colours sit in one palette block ( --kb-palette-* in assets/kokeb/kokeb.css ). Self-CI: actionlint and shellcheck (pinned, SHA-256 verified), shellcheck of the composite action, the permissions contract, the README inputs tables, breaking-change detection, unit tests of the checks (the CI gate, the DCO script and the organisation-standard script included), the theme package's tests and the template site.
docs.title: Added

docs.text: Every reusable workflow sets permissions: {} at the top and the least each job needs; the self-CI enforces both. Every checkout sets persist-credentials: false except the two jobs that push (the release tag and the documentation branch).
docs.title: Security

docs.text: dco ¶ Fail a pull request when any of its commits lacks a Signed-off-by: line that matches the commit's author. dco.yml enforces the Developer Certificate of Origin that every Kokeb Labs repository asks of its contributors. It reads the pull request's commits through the GitHub API with actions/github-script ; it checks out nothing, so no code of the pull request runs. What it does ¶ Lists the commits of the pull request (up to 250, the API's limit; a longer pull request fails with a message). Skips merge commits ( skip_merge_commits ) and commits whose GitHub author is a bot ( allow_bots ). Accepts a commit when one of its Signed-off-by: Name <email> trailers has the author's name and email, compared without case and with runs of spaces collapsed. Fails with one error per commit and a table in the job summary: the commit, its subject, and the sign-off it has (or that it has none). On an event without a pull request (a push, merge_group ) it passes with a notice. Caller ¶ on : pull_request : jobs : dco : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/dco.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : read Put it in the same workflow as the CI gate and list it in the gate's needs , so the sign-off is part of the one required check. Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps dco (DCO) contents: read , pull-requests: read Check the sign-off of every commit Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description allow_bots boolean true Accept commits whose GitHub author is a bot account (type Bot, or a login ending in [bot]), such as Dependabot or github-actions, without a sign-off. skip_merge_commits boolean true Accept merge commits (more than one parent) without a sign-off; they add no authored change of their own. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix no Signed-off-by line The commit was made without -s git commit --amend -s (last commit) or git rebase --signoff <base> , then force-push sign-off is ..., author is ... The trailer names someone else, or another email Set user.name and user.email to the values in the trailer, or sign off again the API listed N of M commits More than 250 commits in one pull request Split the pull request startup_failure The caller does not grant contents: read and pull-requests: read Grant both on the calling job

docs.text: Documentation platform ¶ The pieces every Kokeb Labs documentation site is built from, where each one lives, and how a repository uses them. The pieces ¶ Piece Where What it gives a repository Theme package packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme theme: kokeb (brand, layout, components, light and dark), plugins: [kokeb] (Markdown dialect, validation, repository links, figures, page checks), figkit, the kokeb-docs command and the pinned toolchain Publish workflow ru-mkdocs-publish.yml Strict build, drift checks, Doxygen under api/ , offline link check, Lighthouse budget, screenshots, publish with mike or at the branch root Template templates/mkdocs-site The skeleton of a driver site; the self-CI builds it Migration tool tools/docs-migrate.py The mechanical move from Jekyll, with a --check dry run Guides Migrating to MkDocs , Style guide The procedure, and what the pages contain A repository carries no CSS, templates, hooks or requirements file for its site. The workflow installs the theme package from its own commit, so a caller pinned to @v1 builds with the theme released in v1 . A site in three files ¶ mkdocs.yml site_name : TMC9660 Driver site_description : One sentence on what this is. repo_url : https://github.com/kokeb-labs/driver-tmc9660 theme : name : kokeb plugins : - kokeb - search - awesome-nav docs/.nav.yml orders the pages; .github/workflows/ci-docs-publish.yml calls the workflow ( Quickstart ). The plugin fills in the rest: site_url , repo_name , edit_uri , the Markdown extensions, strict validation and the version selector. Versioned and unversioned sites ¶ Versioned (every repository) Unversioned (the portal, kokeb-labs.github.io ) Addresses https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/<version>/ , root redirects to latest/ https://kokeb-labs.github.io/ Push to main Publishes dev (also latest until the first release) Replaces the site on gh-pages Tag vX.Y.Z Publishes vX.Y.Z , moves latest Nothing Selector Version selector in the header, banner on old versions None Set by Default versioning: false on the workflow; the plugin knows <org>.github.io by itself The kokeb-docs command ¶ Command Does kokeb-docs figures [--check] Builds (or checks) the figkit figures under docs/diagrams/figures/ kokeb-docs gen [--check] Fills (or checks) <!-- generated: name --> regions; repository generators live in tools/docs/generators/ kokeb-docs check Both checks, as CI runs them kokeb-docs screenshots SITE OUT Phone and desktop screenshots, light and dark (needs the [screenshots] extra) kokeb-docs publish-root SITE Commits a built site as the whole deployment branch (unversioned sites) This site uses a generator itself: tools/docs/generators/workflows.py writes the catalogue, the permissions table and every inputs and jobs table from the workflow files. Preview a site locally ¶ python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate pip install "git+https://github.com/kokeb-labs/ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme" mkdocs serve # http://127.0.0.1:8000 mkdocs build --strict -d /tmp/site # what CI runs lychee --offline --include-fragments --index-files index.html --root-dir /tmp/site '/tmp/site/**/*.html' Sites that carry their own copy of the theme ¶ A site that copied overrides/ , a stylesheet under docs/stylesheets/ , tools/docs/ and tools/figkit/ into the repository moves onto the package like this: Set theme: {name: kokeb} and plugins: [kokeb, search, awesome-nav] . Delete the copies and requirements-docs.txt . Change figure modules to from kokeb_mkdocs_theme.figkit import Fig . Move repository-specific generators to tools/docs/generators/ ; they run under kokeb-docs gen . Next: Migrating to MkDocs .

docs.text: ESP-IDF quickstart ¶ Add an ESP32 build to a repository in three files: the app list, the tools and a fifteen-line workflow. What the workflow expects ¶ File Purpose examples/esp32/CMakeLists.txt The ESP-IDF project: idf.py build works in this folder examples/esp32/app_config.yml The apps to build, with the ESP-IDF versions, build types and target examples/esp32/sdkconfig.defaults Kconfig defaults; Kokeb Labs projects set CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 here examples/esp32/scripts/ espidf-tools as a submodule (or let the workflow clone it) examples/esp32 is the Kokeb Labs convention and the path the matrix script looks in first; see The matrix before you put the project anywhere else. FreeRTOS runs at 1000 Hz Kokeb Labs ESP-IDF projects run FreeRTOS at 1000 Hz; kb-core's RTOS timing assumes at least 1 kHz for ms-precision delays. ESP-IDF's default is 100 Hz. The workflow passes no defaults file of its own, so ESP-IDF reads sdkconfig.defaults from the project folder, and a committed sdkconfig takes precedence over it. Put CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 in whichever of the two the project uses. Add the tools as a submodule: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs/espidf-tools.git examples/esp32/scripts List the apps in examples/esp32/app_config.yml : --- metadata : target : esp32c6 idf_versions : [ "release/v5.5" ] build_types : [[ "Debug" , "Release" ]] apps : gpio_test : description : GPIO self-test source_file : GpioTest.cpp Call the workflow from .github/workflows/esp32-examples-build-ci.yml : --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : jobs : build : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts Open a pull request. The run shows one job per app, ESP-IDF version and build type, uploads a fw-<app>-<idf>-<build type> artifact for each and comments a size table on the pull request. Grant the permissions in the calling job A reusable workflow cannot use more permissions than its caller grants. Without pull-requests: write the run fails before any job starts ( startup_failure ). See the permissions contract . Add releases ¶ To attach the firmware to a GitHub Release on every v* tag, add .github/workflows/release.yml : --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-firmware.yml@v1 permissions : actions : read # find the tagged commit's CI run; a private repository refuses it otherwise contents : write # create the release with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml The build must have run on the tagged commit first; see ru-release-firmware . Next: ru-build , every input and what can go wrong.

docs.text: org-standard-check ¶ Check that a repository has the root files every Kokeb Labs repository must carry, and that its licence is MIT. org-standard-check.yml checks out the repository and fails when a required file is missing or empty, or when LICENSE is not the MIT licence. What it checks ¶ Check Passes when README.md the file exists and is not empty LICENSE the file exists and is not empty CHANGELOG.md the file exists and is not empty .github/CODEOWNERS the file exists and is not empty Each path in extra_files the file exists and is not empty MIT licence LICENSE holds the MIT grant, notice and warranty text (line wrapping ignored) and a Copyright (c) <year> <holder> line The result is a table in the job summary and one error annotation per failed check. Caller ¶ jobs : org-standard : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/org-standard-check.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps check (Organisation standard) contents: read actions/checkout ; Required files and the MIT licence Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description extra_files string empty More files that must exist, as paths relative to the repository root separated by spaces or newlines (for example SECURITY.md docs/index.md ). The organisation's own list is always checked. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix required file ... is missing or empty The file is not at that path Add it; CODEOWNERS belongs in .github/ LICENSE is not the MIT licence Another licence, or edited MIT text Use the MIT text with Copyright (c) <year> The Kokeb Labs Authors LICENSE has no 'Copyright (c) <year> <holder>' line The copyright line is missing Add it above the grant

docs.text: Permissions contract ¶ What each reusable workflow needs from its caller, and the rules that keep that list true. Why it matters ¶ A called workflow cannot have more permissions than its caller grants. When a job of a reusable workflow asks for more, GitHub refuses the whole run before any job starts ( startup_failure ), in every repository that calls it. So a workflow here asks for the least it needs, per job, and the README and this page say exactly what that is. What each workflow needs ¶ Grant at least the "Caller grants" column on the calling job, or at the top of the calling workflow. The table is read from the workflow files. Workflow Caller grants Job: permissions dco.yml contents: read , pull-requests: read dco : contents: read , pull-requests: read org-standard-check.yml contents: read check : contents: read ru-attest-release.yml attestations: write , contents: read , id-token: write attest : attestations: write , contents: read , id-token: write ru-build.yml contents: read , pull-requests: write generate-matrix : contents: read build : contents: read size-report : pull-requests: write ru-ci-gate.yml contents: read gate : contents: read ru-cpp-analysis.yml contents: read cppcheck : contents: read ru-cpp-lint.yml contents: read lint : contents: read ru-cross-build.yml contents: read build-cores : contents: read plan : none build : contents: read ru-docs-linkcheck.yml contents: read link-check : contents: read ru-docs-publish.yml contents: write input-validation : none quality-checks : contents: read version-detection : contents: read build : contents: write ru-handbook-check.yml contents: read check : contents: read ru-host-ci.yml contents: read host : contents: read ru-host-quality.yml contents: read gates : contents: read complexity : contents: read coverage : contents: read sanitizers : contents: read fuzz : contents: read ru-markdown-lint.yml contents: read markdownlint : contents: read ru-misra.yml contents: read plan : contents: read scan : contents: read report : contents: read ru-mkdocs-publish.yml contents: write build : contents: read quality : contents: read deploy : contents: write ru-release-firmware.yml actions: read , contents: write release : actions: read , contents: write ru-release-with-artifacts.yml contents: write release : contents: write ru-release.yml contents: write release : contents: write ru-repo-checks.yml contents: read , pull-requests: read checks : contents: read , pull-requests: read ru-template-drift.yml contents: read drift : contents: read ru-yaml-lint.yml contents: read yamllint : contents: read The rules ¶ The self-CI ( check_permissions.py in the workflow contract checks job) fails a pull request when: Rule Why A reusable workflow's top-level permissions: is missing or not {} Nothing is granted by default; permissions are per job, so a read-only job never holds a write token A job of a reusable workflow has no permissions: mapping It would inherit everything the caller granted A workflow's job permissions differ from its row in the README table More breaks callers; less means the table asks for too much A reusable workflow has no row, or a row names no workflow The table is the contract callers read A caller in this repository grants less than the contract The self-tests would hit startup_failure A new permission on an existing workflow is a breaking change: it needs a ### Breaking entry in the changelog and a new major ( Versioning ). The "no bare && tail" rule ¶ GitHub runs run: blocks with bash -e , and a script's exit status is that of its last command. A last line such as [ -n "$X" ] && echo "..." fails the step whenever the condition is false, although -e ignores the same line anywhere else. check_run_tails.py fails any run: block that ends that way; write an if ... fi instead. Next: the workflow catalogue .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Add CI to a Kokeb Labs repository: one workflow file that calls the reusable workflows at @v1 and ends with the gate. One workflow, one required check ¶ Put every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml . Each job calls one reusable workflow and grants exactly the permissions that workflow needs ( Permissions contract ). The last job is the gate. .github/workflows/ci.yml name : CI on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : permissions : contents : read concurrency : group : ci-${{ github.ref }} cancel-in-progress : true jobs : host : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-host-ci.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : preset : host-debug build_dir : build/host-debug markdown : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-markdown-lint.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read ci-gate : name : CI gate needs : [ host , markdown ] # every other job in this workflow if : always() # a skipped required check counts as passing uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : needs_json : ${{ toJSON(needs) }} Then require only the check CI gate / gate in the repository ruleset. Adding, renaming or splitting jobs later needs no change to the ruleset; the gate fails if a job is missing from its needs . Documentation ¶ The documentation site has its own workflow, because it publishes on main and on tags: .github/workflows/ci-docs-publish.yml name : 📚 Docs on : push : branches : [ main ] tags : [ 'v*' ] pull_request : branches : [ main ] permissions : contents : read jobs : docs : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-mkdocs-publish.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write # the publish job pushes gh-pages; pull requests never publish with : doxygen_config : Doxyfile deploy : true Migrating to MkDocs sets up mkdocs.yml and docs/ for it. When a run fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure , no job started The calling job grants less than the workflow needs Grant the permissions in the contract startup_failure after an upgrade to a new major An input was removed or made required Read the ### Breaking notes in the changelog The gate fails with "not in needs" A job was added without adding it to the gate's needs Add it to needs A fix merged here does not reach a re-run "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the revision of the first run Start a new run (push, Run workflow , or reopen the pull request) Next: Versioning .

docs.text: ru-attest-release ¶ Sign build provenance for every file of a published release. ru-attest-release.yml runs after ru-release or ru-release-firmware (or the deprecated ru-release-with-artifacts ). It downloads the release's files, checks each against the release's SHA256SUMS , and creates a GitHub artifact attestation for every file that SHA256SUMS lists: an SLSA build-provenance statement, signed through Sigstore and stored on the repository. Anyone can then check that a file they downloaded came from this repository's release workflow at a given commit. It is a separate workflow because it needs id-token: write and attestations: write . GitHub refuses to start a called workflow when any of its jobs asks for more than its caller grants, so adding the job to the release workflows would break their existing callers. Attestations need a public repository, or GitHub Enterprise Cloud for a private one. Caller ¶ Add a job after the release job, in the same workflow: jobs : release : # ... ru-release or ru-release-firmware ... attest : needs : release uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-attest-release.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read id-token : write attestations : write with : tag_name : ${{ github.ref_name }} # or the tag the release job used Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps attest (Attest release files) attestations: write , contents: read , id-token: write Download the release files and check them against SHA256SUMS; Attest every file in SHA256SUMS Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description tag_name string empty Tag of the published release to attest (defaults to github.ref_name) Check a download ¶ gh release download v1.2.0 -R kokeb-labs/driver-as5047u -D v1.2.0 && cd v1.2.0 sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS gh attestation verify as5047u-1.2.0.tar.gz -R kokeb-labs/driver-as5047u \ --signer-workflow kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-attest-release.yml gh attestation verify checks that the file's digest was signed by this workflow, running for that repository, and prints the commit and the workflow run. Repeat it for each file you use. What it proves: the release workflow of the repository published these exact files at the tagged commit. The firmware zips are built by ru-build in CI and released by ru-release-firmware only after that CI run passed on the tagged commit. The attestation is signed in the release job, not in the build job. docs.text: Sign build provenance for every file of a published release. ru-attest-release.yml runs after ru-release or ru-release-firmware (or the deprecated ru-release-with-artifacts ). It downloads the release's files, checks each against the release's SHA256SUMS , and creates a GitHub artifact attestation for every file that SHA256SUMS lists: an SLSA build-provenance statement, signed through Sigstore and stored on the repository. Anyone can then check that a file they downloaded came from this repository's release workflow at a given commit. It is a separate workflow because it needs id-token: write and attestations: write . GitHub refuses to start a called workflow when any of its jobs asks for more than its caller grants, so adding the job to the release workflows would break their existing callers. Attestations need a public repository, or GitHub Enterprise Cloud for a private one.

docs.text: ru-build ¶ Build every ESP32 example app of a repository across ESP-IDF versions and build types, upload the firmware and report its size on pull requests. File: .github/workflows/ru-build.yml Caller ¶ --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : jobs : build : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts max_dec_total : "0" Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description project_dir string required Path to the ESP-IDF project (contains CMakeLists.txt) project_tools_dir string empty Path to project tools directory (contains scripts directly). Leave empty to auto-detect. clean_build boolean false Skip caches for a clean build. auto_clone_tools boolean true Auto-clone tools repo if project_tools_dir is missing group_build_types boolean true Build every build type of an app and IDF version in one job (default), so the runner is prepared and the ESP-IDF image pulled once per app instead of once per build type. false keeps one job per build type. idf_install string native How the job gets ESP-IDF. native (default): a shallow clone of the IDF version with the tools of the matrix target only, kept in the Actions cache by IDF commit (about 1.1 GB; a warm restore takes seconds, against a minute or more to pull the 9 GB espressif/idf image). docker: the espressif/idf image through espressif/esp-idf-ci-action, as before. max_dec_total string 0 Maximum total dec size in bytes for size budget enforcement (0 to disable) Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Runs Permissions generate-matrix always contents: read build once per matrix entry, fail-fast: false , 30 min limit contents: read size-report pull requests only pull-requests: write generate-matrix checks out with submodules, finds the project tools (below), runs generate_matrix.py and outputs the matrix. build builds every build type of one app and IDF version ( group_build_types ): it checks out, restores the pip and compiler (ccache) caches (skipped with clean_build ) and installs the tools' requirements.txt . With idf_install: native (default) it resolves the IDF version to a commit, restores ~/esp-idf and ~/.espressif for the matrix target from the cache keyed by that commit (or clones the IDF and runs install.sh <target> once when the key is new), installs a pinned, hash-checked ccache and runs build_app.sh for each build type. With idf_install: docker it frees runner disk space when short, pulls espressif/idf:<version> (4 attempts, 10 / 30 / 60 s apart) and runs build_app.sh inside the image with espressif/esp-idf-ci-action . Either way it uploads the build folders. Measured on driver-pcal9555 (Debug and Release of one app): native, warm cache, 93 s per job; native, new IDF commit, about 190 s; docker with a warm ccache, 175 s. The image is 9.4 GB for every target; the native cache holds one target, about 1.1 GB. - size-report downloads every fw-* artifact, writes a size table from size.info / size.txt , comments it on the pull request and enforces max_dec_total when it is not 0 . The caller grants the union: contents: read and pull-requests: write . See the permissions contract . Finding the project tools ¶ The generate-matrix job needs generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh from espidf-tools . It looks, in this order: Case Path used project_tools_dir set That path; the job fails if it does not exist (no clone) project_tools_dir empty and <project_dir>/espidf-tools exists That folder Otherwise espidf-tools at the repository root, cloned from main (depth 1) when it is missing and auto_clone_tools is true A submodule is the reproducible choice: the clone follows the tools' main branch. The matrix ¶ generate_matrix.py reads app_config.yml and emits one entry per app, ESP-IDF version and build type: app_config.yml Effect metadata.idf_versions ESP-IDF branches or tags, for example release/v5.5 ; default release/v5.5 metadata.build_types One list per IDF version, by index: [["Debug", "Release"], ["Debug"]] metadata.target Chip passed to the build, default esp32c6 apps.<name>.idf_versions , apps.<name>.build_types Per-app overrides; a flat build_types list applies to every version apps.<name>.ci_enabled: false Leaves the app out of CI ci_config.exclude_combinations Entries whose keys all match are dropped, for example {app_name: x, build_type: Release} Where app_config.yml is found The workflow runs generate_matrix.py without --project-path , so the script looks for examples/esp32/app_config.yml from the repository root, then for app_config.yml in the folder above the script. Keep the project in examples/esp32 , or keep the tools inside the project folder, so both point at the same file. Artifacts ¶ Each build uploads <project_dir>/build* as fw-<app_name>-<idf_version_docker>-<build_type> , for example fw-gpio_test-release-v5.5-Debug , kept for 7 days. build_app.sh writes size.info and size.txt into the build folder; the size report reads them. The upload runs even when the build fails, so a failed build's logs are in the artifact. Size report and budget ¶ On pull requests the size-report job comments a table with one row per build (app, IDF, target, build type and the idf.py size summary). Set max_dec_total to a byte count to fail the job when any build's total dec size is larger; 0 turns the check off. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure , no job ran The calling job grants less than contents: read , pull-requests: write Add the permissions to the calling job Project tools directory not found project_tools_dir points at a missing folder, or the submodule was not added Add the submodule, or leave project_tools_dir empty to clone Required script ... not found The tools folder is not espidf-tools, or is an old copy Update the submodule Configuration file not found No app_config.yml where generate_matrix.py looks (see the warning above) Move the project to examples/esp32 or the tools into the project Could not pull espressif/idf:... after 4 attempts Docker Hub outage, or an IDF version with no image Check the version name; start a new run No build directory found! build_app.sh failed before creating build* Read the build step log; reproduce locally with build_app.sh Size budget exceeded A build's dec total is above max_dec_total Shrink the firmware or raise the budget A fix here does not apply "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the workflow revision of the first run Start a new run (see Versioning ) Next: ru-release-firmware , which ships these artifacts.

docs.text: ru-ci-gate ¶ One required status check per repository: it passes only when every other CI job passed. ru-ci-gate.yml turns the results of all jobs in a workflow into a single check. A repository's ruleset then requires that one check instead of a list of job names that has to be updated whenever jobs are added, renamed or split. Caller pattern ¶ Add the gate as the last job of the CI workflow: jobs : build : # ... lint : # ... docs : # ... ci-gate : name : CI gate needs : [ build , lint , docs ] # every other job in this workflow if : always() # required, see below uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : needs_json : ${{ toJSON(needs) }} allow_skipped : docs # optional: jobs that may be skipped Then, in the repository ruleset (or branch protection), require only the status check named: CI gate / gate GitHub names checks from a called workflow <calling job name> / <called job name> , so with name: CI gate on the calling job the check is always CI gate / gate , in every repository. Rules ¶ The gate passes if and only if every job in needs finished with success , or with skipped and is listed in allow_skipped . failure , cancelled , and an unlisted skipped all fail it. if: always() is required. Without it, a failing job causes the gate to be skipped, and a skipped required check counts as passing . Every job must be in needs . A job outside needs can fail without failing the gate. With verify_needs: true (the default) the gate reads the calling workflow file and fails if either rule above is broken. It also fails if allow_skipped names a job that is not in needs , which catches typos. Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description needs_json string required The caller's needs context as JSON: the expression toJSON(needs) allow_skipped string empty Jobs (ids from needs ) that may be skipped without failing the gate, separated by commas, spaces or newlines. Every other job must succeed. verify_needs boolean true Read the calling workflow file and fail if a job is missing from the gate's needs , or if the gate job lacks if: always() . Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps gate (gate) contents: read Evaluate needed jobs contents: read is used to read the calling workflow file. Jobs that run conditionally ¶ A job that is skipped by design, for example a deploy job that runs only on main , goes in allow_skipped . A job that is skipped because something it needs failed is reported as skipped too. That case is still caught: the failed upstream job is itself in needs , so the gate fails on it. A job that calls dco.yml only on pull requests ( if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' ) is skipped on every push, so it goes in allow_skipped . ru-repo-checks runs DCO as a step that passes with nothing to check outside a pull request: its job always runs and needs no allow_skipped entry.

docs.text: ru-cpp-analysis ¶ Run cppcheck over source folders, without a build, and keep the report as an artifact. ru-cpp-analysis.yml runs cppcheck in a container ( ghcr.io/facthunder/cppcheck ) over paths . It needs no compile database, so it suits header-only drivers and repositories without a host build; with a CMake build, ru-host-ci runs cppcheck on the compiler's own database instead. What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Runs cppcheck with --enable=<enable> , --std=<std> , inline suppressions, -i for each exclude path, and --force / --max-configs when set. missingIncludeSystem and unmatchedSuppression are suppressed, because system headers are not mounted. Uploads cppcheck_report.xml and the console output as the cppcheck-report artifact (14 days). With strict: true , fails the job when the report is not empty. Caller ¶ jobs : cppcheck : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-analysis.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : paths : "src inc" std : c++20 strict : true Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps cppcheck contents: read actions/checkout ; Install cppcheck; Run cppcheck; Upload report; Fail on findings (strict) Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description paths string src inc examples Dirs to analyze (space-separated) std string c++20 C++ standard strict boolean false Fail the job when cppcheck reports a finding (severity other than information) exclude string empty Paths to exclude (space-separated) enable string warning,style,performance,portability,information Checks to enable (comma-separated: all,warning,style,performance, portability,information,unusedFunction,missingInclude) force boolean false Force checking even with incomplete analysis max_configs number 0 Maximum configs to check (for template-heavy code, 0=unlimited) artifact_name string cppcheck-report Name of the uploaded report artifact (unique per call when a run calls this more than once) When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix The job passes although cppcheck printed findings strict is false (the default) Set strict: true once the findings are fixed "Too many #ifdef configurations" Template- or macro-heavy code Set max_configs , or force: true A path is not found paths and exclude are relative to the repository root, space-separated Check each folder exists in the checkout

docs.text: ru-cpp-lint ¶ Check C and C++ formatting with clang-format and lint with clang-tidy, with results as annotations on the pull request. ru-cpp-lint.yml runs clang-format 20.1.8 and clang-tidy 20.1.0 with the repository's own .clang-format and .clang-tidy . Both come from LLVM's builds published on PyPI, pinned and checked against their SHA-256, so no install script or third-party action runs. With cmake_args , it configures the project first and gives clang-tidy the CMake compile database, so clang-tidy sees the include paths and defines the compiler sees; without it, clang-tidy guesses and cannot find the project's own headers. Every finding fails the job unless fail_on_findings is false. What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Links clang_format_config and clang_tidy_config to .clang-format and .clang-tidy at the root when they live elsewhere (the Kokeb Labs layout keeps them in _config/ ). A missing file is a warning, not an error. Installs the pinned clang-format and clang-tidy. Selects the files: git ls-files with extensions , without ignore , and only the files a pull request changes when files_changed_only is true. With cmake_args , configures CMake with CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON into build-clang-tidy/ . Runs clang-format ( --dry-run -Werror ) and clang-tidy on every selected file in parallel. Each finding is an annotation on its line; the run summary has a table and the clang-tidy findings. Compiler warnings that clang-tidy echoes as clang-diagnostic-* are left to the build, except hard errors. Fails when any file has a finding ( fail_on_findings , default true). findings is the number of such files. thread_comments and lines_changed_only are still accepted but ignored: whole files are always checked. docs.text: Check C and C++ formatting with clang-format and lint with clang-tidy, with results as annotations on the pull request. ru-cpp-lint.yml runs clang-format 20.1.8 and clang-tidy 20.1.0 with the repository's own .clang-format and .clang-tidy . Both come from LLVM's builds published on PyPI, pinned and checked against their SHA-256, so no install script or third-party action runs. With cmake_args , it configures the project first and gives clang-tidy the CMake compile database, so clang-tidy sees the include paths and defines the compiler sees; without it, clang-tidy guesses and cannot find the project's own headers. Every finding fails the job unless fail_on_findings is false.

docs.text: Checks out the repository. Links clang_format_config and clang_tidy_config to .clang-format and .clang-tidy at the root when they live elsewhere (the Kokeb Labs layout keeps them in _config/ ). A missing file is a warning, not an error. Installs the pinned clang-format and clang-tidy. Selects the files: git ls-files with extensions , without ignore , and only the files a pull request changes when files_changed_only is true. With cmake_args , configures CMake with CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON into build-clang-tidy/ . Runs clang-format ( --dry-run -Werror ) and clang-tidy on every selected file in parallel. Each finding is an annotation on its line; the run summary has a table and the clang-tidy findings. Compiler warnings that clang-tidy echoes as clang-diagnostic-* are left to the build, except hard errors. Fails when any file has a finding ( fail_on_findings , default true). findings is the number of such files. thread_comments and lines_changed_only are still accepted but ignored: whole files are always checked.

docs.text: ru-cross-build ¶ Compile a CMake target for microcontroller cores with the GNU Arm Embedded toolchain, so code that claims to run on any MCU is shown to compile for one on every pull request. ru-cross-build.yml builds every core in cores in one job, one core after the other, each in its own build directory and log group ( per_core_jobs: true gives one job per core instead): Installs Arm's GNU toolchain release 14.3.rel1 (GCC 14, newlib, libstdc++), checked against the SHA-256 Arm publishes with it, so every run uses the same identified compiler. Writes a CMake toolchain file for the core ( -mcpu , -mthumb , the float ABI and FPU) with CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE STATIC_LIBRARY , so configuring needs no linker script. Configures with that toolchain at MinSizeRel and builds only build_target . The project's own flags still apply: a Kokeb driver's test flags are -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -Werror and the full warning set. Writes the objects' text , data and bss sizes to the run summary. A core that fails to build does not stop the others; the job fails at the end and names every core that failed. The toolchain is downloaded once for all of them, and a private repository is billed one job, rounded up to a whole minute, instead of one per core and one for checking the list. Core Flags cortex-m0plus -mcpu=cortex-m0plus -mthumb -mfloat-abi=soft cortex-m3 -mcpu=cortex-m3 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=soft cortex-m4f -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 cortex-m7f -mcpu=cortex-m7 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv5-d16 cortex-m33f -mcpu=cortex-m33 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv5-sp-d16 The default is cortex-m0plus cortex-m4f cortex-m7f : the smallest core without an FPU, and the two most common cores with one. What to build ¶ The target must compile code that instantiates the driver; a header-only INTERFACE library compiles nothing. A Kokeb driver passes <chip>_optimised_build , the object library that compiles every test source, and with it every operation of the driver against the mock port, at -O2 with the strict flags. Nothing is linked, so no linker script or startup code is needed. Caller ¶ jobs : cross : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cross-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : build_target : mychip_optimised_build cmake_args : "-DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON" Add the job to the CI gate's needs .

docs.text: ru-docs-linkcheck ¶ Check every link in a repository's Markdown, external ones included, with lychee. ru-docs-linkcheck.yml runs lychee over Markdown files in the repository. It complements ru-mkdocs-publish , whose link check runs offline on the built site: this one also follows external links, and checks Markdown that is not part of a site (READMEs, examples). What it does ¶ Checks out the repository, with submodules when checkout_recursive is set. Works out the repository's own Pages site ( https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/ ) and leaves links to it out of the check on pull requests, where the pages a change links to are not published yet, and on other events while its latest/ (the root, for <owner>.github.io ) does not answer, as before a repository's first MkDocs publish. Turn this off with exclude_own_site: false . Runs lychee over paths with the timeout, retries and exclusions set by the inputs, and a lychee.toml when config_file names one. Caller ¶ jobs : links : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-docs-linkcheck.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : paths : "docs/**/*.md *.md" Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps link-check contents: read Checkout repository; Own documentation site; Restore lychee; Install lychee (pinned, hash-checked); Link check with Lychee Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description checkout_recursive boolean false Checkout submodules recursively (useful for projects with documentation in submodules) paths string docs/** *.md **/docs/** Space-separated paths to check for broken links fail_on_errors boolean true Fail the workflow if broken links are found timeout string 10 Timeout in seconds for each link check max_retries string 3 Maximum number of retries per request retry_wait_time string 1 Minimum wait time in seconds between retries exclude_private boolean true Exclude private/internal links exclude_mail boolean true Exclude mailto links verbose boolean false Enable verbose output config_file string empty Path to lychee.toml config file (optional) exclude_own_site boolean true Skip links to this repository's own GitHub Pages site (https:// .github.io/ /) on pull requests, where the pages a change links to are not published yet, and on other events while the site's latest/ version (the root, for .github.io) does not answer yet, as before a repository's first MkDocs publish. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix A link to the repository's own site under /latest/ fails on main The site answers, but the page is new and not published yet It passes after the publish; or exclude that path in lychee.toml A site that blocks bots answers 403 or 429 Rate limits or bot protection Exclude the host in lychee.toml Links into a submodule fail The submodule was not checked out Set checkout_recursive: true Intermittent timeouts A slow host Raise timeout or max_retries

docs.text: ru-docs-publish (legacy) ¶ Build a Jekyll site with Doxygen and publish it to gh-pages in version folders: the documentation pipeline that ru-mkdocs-publish replaces. Being replaced New sites use ru-mkdocs-publish . Repositories still on this workflow move with Migrating to MkDocs . This workflow keeps working for them under @v1 . What it does ¶ Event Path pull_request , pull_request_target , merge_group Build only: input validation, quality checks, Doxygen, the Jekyll build and the link check; the site is uploaded as the docs-html artifact ( artifact_name ). Never deploys, whatever deploy_pages says Push to main Builds and, with deploy_pages: true , publishes to gh-pages/development/ Push to release/v* or a v* tag Builds and publishes to gh-pages/vX.Y.Z/ Other branches Builds a preview version On gh-pages , each version folder holds the Jekyll site with the Doxygen HTML under api/ ; Doxygen output is also kept under doxs/<version>/ . The root index.html redirects to the newest release (or development ), and version_selector.html lists the versions. A single step, "Decide whether to deploy", decides whether anything is published, and every deploy step reads it. Caller ¶ on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : jobs : docs : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-docs-publish.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write # required on pull requests too: GitHub checks every job's permissions before the run with : doxygen_config : _config/Doxyfile jekyll_enabled : true jekyll_source : "." jekyll_config : _config/_config.yml deploy_pages : true # pull requests still never deploy Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps input-validation none Validate workflow inputs quality-checks contents: read Checkout repository; Setup Node.js for quality tools; Cache pip dependencies; Install quality tools; Run YAML linting; Run markdown linting; Run spell checking version-detection contents: read Checkout repository; Detect version and strategy build contents: write Checkout repository; Check for Doxygen configuration; Restore Doxygen; Install Doxygen (pinned version); Check for pre-installed Graphviz; Install Graphviz (Optimized); Setup Ruby (bundler cache); Setup Node.js; Resolve Doxygen HTML output directory; Cache pip dependencies; Cache Node.js dependencies; Cache Jekyll dependencies; Cache Doxygen build artifacts; Install Jekyll dependencies; Validate Jekyll configuration; Install Node.js tools; Install YAML linting tools; Generate Doxygen documentation with versioning; Stage Doxygen into Jekyll (if enabled); Manage Doxygen versioned artifacts; Quality checks summary; Caching status summary; Generate version-specific configuration; Build Jekyll site; Restore lychee; Install lychee (pinned, hash-checked); Link check with Lychee; Prepare deployment artifacts; Upload documentation artifacts; Decide whether to deploy; Deploy Jekyll site to GitHub Pages; Deploy Doxygen artifacts to GitHub Pages; Update root redirect and version selector Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description checkout_recursive boolean false Checkout submodules recursively (useful for projects with documentation in submodules) run_link_check boolean true Run documentation link checker link_check_paths string **/*.md Space-separated paths to check for broken links link_check_config string empty Path to lychee.toml config file (optional) verbose boolean false Enable verbose output for link checking yamllint_config string _config/.yamllint Path to yamllint configuration file run_markdown_lint boolean false Run markdown linting on documentation files markdown_lint_paths string **/*.md Glob patterns for markdown files to lint markdown_lint_config string _config/.markdownlint.json Path to markdownlint configuration file run_spell_check boolean false Run spell checking on documentation files spell_check_paths string **/*.md Glob patterns for files to spell check spell_check_config string .cspell.json Path to cspell configuration file deployment_branch string gh-pages Branch name for deployment (required for versioned documentation) deploy_pages boolean true Deploy to GitHub Pages. Ignored on pull_request, pull_request_target and merge_group events, which always take the PR build path (build and upload the docs-html artifact, no deploy). artifact_name string docs-html Name of the uploaded site artifact (set it when calling this workflow more than once in one run) doxygen_config string Doxyfile Path to Doxyfile (relative to repo root) - output directory auto-detected from OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and HTML_OUTPUT settings doxygen_working_directory string . Directory to execute Doxygen from (defaults to repository root). Relative paths in the Doxyfile are resolved against this directory. doxygen_fail_on_warnings boolean false Treat Doxygen warnings as errors in CI jekyll_enabled boolean false Enable Jekyll static site generation for enhanced documentation presentation jekyll_config string _config.yml Comma-separated list of Jekyll configuration files (e.g., "_config.yml,_config_prod.yml") jekyll_source string docs Jekyll source directory containing your site files jekyll_destination string _site Jekyll build destination directory for generated site jekyll_environment string production Jekyll environment (development, production, staging) - affects which config files are loaded jekyll_safe boolean true Run in safe mode (disables custom plugins, used by GitHub Pages) - CI Recommended jekyll_plugins_dir string empty Comma-separated list of plugin directories (--plugins option) jekyll_layouts_dir string empty Layout directory (--layouts option) jekyll_verbose boolean false Enable verbose output during Jekyll build - CI Recommended for debugging jekyll_strict_front_matter boolean true Cause build to fail if there is a YAML syntax error in front matter - CI Recommended jekyll_drafts boolean false Include draft posts in the build (useful for development) jekyll_future boolean false Include future-dated posts in the build jekyll_unpublished boolean false Include unpublished posts in the build jekyll_incremental boolean false Enable incremental builds for faster development (may cause issues in CI) jekyll_lsi boolean false Enable LSI (Latent Semantic Indexing) for related posts jekyll_limit_posts string empty Limit the number of posts to parse and publish jekyll_profile boolean false Enable profiling output to show build performance (reduces build time) jekyll_quiet boolean false Suppress normal output during Jekyll build (reduces debugging info) jekyll_trace boolean false Show full backtrace when an error occurs (debug only) When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix "Validate Jekyll configuration" fails jekyll_config or jekyll_source points at nothing Paths are relative to the repository root; the config may live in a subfolder of the source The site has no styling baseurl in _config.yml does not match /<repo> Set baseurl: "/<repo>" without a trailing slash Doxygen output folder missing OUTPUT_DIRECTORY 's parent does not exist The workflow creates it; check doxygen_working_directory Nothing published from main deploy_pages is false Pass deploy_pages: true (or a repository-variable gate)

docs.text: ru-handbook-check ¶ Check a repository against the Kokeb Labs handbook rules that a script can decide, and report every finding by rule ID. The declaration ¶ Each repository says what it is in .kokeb/handbook.yml : --- handbook : "1.0" # the handbook release it follows kind : driver # driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs or template level : high # standard, high or safety waivers : # optional - rule : KB-DOC-004 reason : Doxygen comments for the v2 register API land with #41. approved_by : "@N3b3x" until : 2027-01-31 A rule applies when the repository's kind is in the rule's scope and its level is at or above the rule's lowest level. What it checks ¶ Rule Check KB-REPO-002 The declaration exists and names a handbook release, a kind and a level KB-REPO-003 Every waiver names a handbook rule, a reason, an approver and a date that has not passed KB-REPO-005 The root of a driver holds only the committed entries ADR-0011 allows KB-REPO-018 driver.yml has name, version, bus, mcus, peripheral and kb_core_min, matching cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake KB-CPP-001 The library requires C++20 and compiler extensions are not turned on KB-BLD-002 No file(GLOB) in CMake outside tests/ and examples/ KB-CPP-002 No throw , try , catch , typeid or dynamic_cast in inc/ and src/ KB-CPP-003 No new , delete , malloc and friends, or heap-owning smart pointers in inc/ and src/ KB-ARCH-011 No virtual in a driver (ADR-0016) KB-CPP-012 Driver headers include only the target library subset; other target code includes no allocating, throwing or OS header (ADR-0017) KB-REPO-016 No generated sdkconfig is committed (ADR-0018) KB-DOC-035 No PDF is committed under docs/ (ADR-0019) Code checks read only committed files, with comments and string literals blanked out first, so a word in a comment or a message never counts. = delete and placement new are not heap use. How a finding counts ¶ Error (fails the job): the rule is active, or its enforce_from date has passed. Warning : the rule is still proposed and its enforce_from date is ahead, or it is a should rule. Notice : a valid waiver covers the rule; the notice quotes the waiver. Each finding is an annotation on its file and line with the rule's ID, title and a link to its page, and the run summary has the full table. Where the rules come from ¶ The checker and rules.json , a snapshot of the handbook's rules exported by the handbook's own tooling, live in tools/handbook_check/ in this repository. The workflow checks them out at its own commit, so a caller on @v1 always gets a checker and a rule set that belong together. Caller ¶ jobs : handbook : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-handbook-check.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read Add the job to the CI gate's needs .

docs.text: ru-host-ci ¶ Build, test and analyse a CMake project on the host, with clang-tidy 18 and cppcheck over the compiler's own compile database. ru-host-ci.yml runs the native (host) half of a C/C++ project's CI in one job: Configure. Uses cmake --preset <preset> when preset is set, otherwise cmake -S <source_dir> -B <build_dir> -G Ninja . Either way it passes -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON . Build. Runs cmake --build <build_dir> --parallel . Test. Runs ctest --test-dir <build_dir> --output-on-failure . Select files. Picks translation units from compile_commands.json . A unit is analysed if its path relative to the repository root matches tidy_paths . Units that match exclude_paths and anything generated in the build tree are dropped. The selection is written as a filtered database, so both analysers see exactly the same files. Analyse. Runs clang-tidy 18 ( -p <build_dir> ) and cppcheck ( --project=<filtered database> ) on that set. Both see the include paths and defines the compiler sees, so no configuration is guessed. Report. Findings appear as annotations. The reports, the file list and the database are uploaded as an artifact. With fail_on_findings: true (the default), any finding fails the job. clang-tidy exits 0 even when it prints warnings, so the workflow counts file:line:col: warning|error: ... [check] lines itself. It ignores compiler warnings echoed as clang-diagnostic-* , except clang-diagnostic-error . cppcheck findings are lines of severity error, warning, performance, portability or style; information lines (analysis limits) do not count. Minimal caller ¶ jobs : host : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-host-ci.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : preset : host-debug build_dir : build/host-debug # the preset's binaryDir, from the repo root tidy_paths : "^(src|include|apps)/" cppcheck_suppressions : tools/lint/cppcheck-suppressions.txt Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description preset string empty CMake configure preset (from CMakePresets.json in source_dir). Empty: configure with -S source_dir -B build_dir. source_dir string . CMake source directory, relative to the repository root build_dir string build/host Build directory, relative to the repository root. With a preset this must be the preset's binaryDir; compile_commands.json is read from here. cmake_args string empty Extra arguments for the configure step (space separated) build_type string Debug CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE when no preset is used run_tests boolean true Run ctest after the build ctest_args string empty Extra arguments for ctest (space separated) tidy_paths string empty Python regular expression matched (re.search) against each translation unit's path relative to the repository root. Only matching files are given to clang-tidy and cppcheck. Empty: every file in the database. exclude_paths string (^|/)(third_party|external|vendor|_deps)/ Python regular expression; translation units whose relative path matches are never analysed, and findings in matching files are not counted. The build directory is always excluded. run_clang_tidy boolean true Run clang-tidy 18 on the selected files clang_tidy_config string empty Path to a .clang-tidy file. Empty: clang-tidy's normal lookup from each source file run_cppcheck boolean true Run cppcheck on the selected files cppcheck_suppressions string empty Path to a cppcheck --suppressions-list file (optional) cppcheck_enable string warning,performance,portability cppcheck --enable value fail_on_findings boolean true Fail the job when clang-tidy or cppcheck report findings apt_packages string empty Extra apt packages to install before configuring (space separated) submodules string false actions/checkout submodules value: false, true or recursive runs_on string ubuntu-24.04 Runner label (Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, for clang-tidy-18 from apt) artifact_name string host-ci-reports Name of the uploaded report artifact Outputs: tidy_findings and cppcheck_findings , the counts of findings (empty when a tool did not run). Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps host (build, test, analyse) contents: read actions/checkout ; Install toolchain and analysers; Configure (compile_commands.json exported); Build; Test (ctest); Select files to analyse; clang-tidy 18; cppcheck; Upload reports; Enforce zero findings Self-test ¶ ci-host-ci.yml runs the workflow twice on tests/fixtures/host-ci : with the preset on clean code, where it must pass with fail_on_findings: true (the vendored file with a defect is excluded by the default exclude_paths ); through -S/-B with seeded defects, where both analysers must report findings. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix compile_commands.json not found build_dir is not the preset's binaryDir Set build_dir to the preset's binaryDir , from the repository root clang-tidy reports errors in third-party headers The headers are not under an excluded path Extend exclude_paths , or mark them SYSTEM in CMake cppcheck reports a finding the code means A known false positive Add it to the cppcheck_suppressions file with the path No files analysed tidy_paths matches nothing Check the regex against paths relative to the repository root
