docs.text: ru-host-quality ¶ Complexity, coverage and sanitizer gates for a CMake C/C++ project, with the limits the Kokeb Labs handbook sets for each assurance level (ADR-0020). ru-host-quality.yml runs three independent checks: Check Tool Measures Fails when complexity lizard 1.24.1 Modified cyclomatic complexity (a whole switch counts once), lines of code and parameters of every function in library_paths a function is over a limit coverage GCC 14 --coverage , gcovr 8.7 Line, branch and, when the level asks for it, MC/DC coverage ( -fcondition-coverage ) of library_paths by the tests a figure is below its floor sanitizers clang, AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer The tests built with -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all any report, or a failing test They run as steps of one job. Each check runs whether or not an earlier one failed, fails the job on its own limits, writes its own summary and uploads its own report artifact ( <artifact_name>-complexity , <artifact_name>-coverage ), as separate jobs would; a private repository is billed one job, rounded up to a whole minute, instead of four. separate_jobs: true runs each check in a job of its own, with the same steps. With fuzz_cmake_args set, libFuzzer (clang 18, ASan, UBSan) runs every fuzz_<name> target for the level's seconds (60, 120, 600), seeded from tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_<name>/ and a cached corpus. Fuzzing is long, so it is always a job of its own, in parallel with the checks above. Python tools are installed from pinned versions checked against their SHA-256 hashes, and each version was at least three weeks old when it was pinned. Limits by level ¶ Limit standard high safety Cyclomatic complexity (modified) 15 15 10 Function length (lines of code) 80 60 60 Parameters 7 6 6 Line coverage reported 85% 100% Branch coverage reported 75% 100% MC/DC coverage not measured reported 100% Every limit can be overridden with an input ( max_ccn , max_length , max_params , min_line , min_branch , min_condition ); an override should match a waiver or deviation recorded in the repository. What is counted ¶ Library code only. library_paths (default inc src ) names it. Tests, examples and tools are not measured for complexity and do not count towards coverage. Every C and C++ file, header-only implementations included. The complexity job lists .c , .cc , .cpp , .cxx , .h , .hh , .hpp , .hxx , .ipp , .tpp and .inl files under library_paths itself: lizard alone skips .ipp , .tpp and .inl files in a directory, which is where a header-only driver keeps its code. Per source line, all template instances together. A header-only driver is a class template, compiled once for every port type a test or example uses. gcovr's --merge-lines counts a line, branch or condition as covered when any instance ran it: coverage measures the source, as a structural-coverage objective does, not how many copies the compiler made. Without it, an example that instantiates the driver with its own port and runs only the happy path would count every failure path a second time, as uncovered. Only code that ran. Coverage reads the data of test binaries that executed. A compile-only target (for example an optimised build that exists to prove the code compiles at -O2 ) has no data and would otherwise count every line as missed. No exception branches. The compiler's exception-handling branches and unreachable branches are excluded: Kokeb code builds without exceptions. Minimal caller ¶ jobs : quality : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-host-quality.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : level : high cmake_args : "-DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON" Add the job to the CI gate's needs . The reports (lizard's full table, gcovr's HTML, Cobertura XML and JSON summary) are uploaded as artifacts, and the figures appear in the run summary. Outputs ¶ complexity_findings , line_coverage , branch_coverage and condition_coverage let a later job record the figures, for example in a release's evidence package.

docs.text: ru-markdown-lint ¶ Lint Markdown with markdownlint-cli2 against the repository's own rules. ru-markdown-lint.yml runs markdownlint-cli2 over globs with config_file . The Kokeb Labs layout keeps the rules in _config/.markdownlint.json ; a site on the documentation platform allows the theme's HTML and indented admonition bodies ( MD033 , MD046 and MD041 off). What it does ¶ Mode How Exclusions Default ( use_docker: false ) The official markdownlint-cli2 action Through the config file's ignores use_docker: true markdownlint-cli2 in a container, file list filtered first exclude_patterns (substring match) as well With fix: true the linter rewrites what it can fix, in the job's checkout only; nothing is committed. Outputs: result , files_checked , issues_found . Caller ¶ jobs : markdown : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-markdown-lint.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : config_file : _config/.markdownlint.json Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps markdownlint (Markdown Lint) contents: read Checkout code; Run markdownlint (Official Action - Simple); Process results (Official Action); Run markdownlint (Docker - Full Control with Excludes); Consolidate outputs Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description globs string **/*.md Space-separated list of glob patterns to check (default: all markdown files) config_file string _config/.markdownlint.json Path to markdownlint configuration file (default: _config/.markdownlint.json) exclude_patterns string .git/**,node_modules/**,venv/**,.venv/**,_site/**,**/espidf-tools/** Comma-separated patterns to exclude from checking use_docker boolean false Use Docker container instead of official action (for more control) fix boolean false Automatically fix fixable issues (equivalent to --fix flag) separator string empty Separator to use between glob patterns (default: space) When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix MD033 on every page of a documentation site Material components are HTML Turn MD033 off, or allow the theme's elements MD046 on admonitions Admonition bodies are indented Turn MD046 off Files in a submodule or build folder are linted The default glob is **/*.md Add them to the config's ignores , or use use_docker with exclude_patterns

docs.text: ru-misra ¶ Check C++ code against MISRA C++:2023 with the validated open-source toolchain, and get a per-guideline report. ru-misra.yml builds the caller twice, for the host and for a Cortex-M core, each time traced by CodeQL. It runs the MISRA C++:2023 queries of the CodeQL coding-standards pack and the Kokeb C++20 profile pack on both databases. It applies the handbook's deviation records, and runs clang-tidy's validated checks and cppcheck on the same compile databases. Every tool comes from tools/misra/toolchain.json at the workflow's commit, pinned by version and SHA-256. The tool validation plan explains why each tool can be trusted for what it decides. Licence: open-source code only The CodeQL Terms and Conditions license analysis of an Open Source Codebase , code released under an OSI-approved licence, and CI use when it is hosted on GitHub.com. Any other codebase needs a paid GitHub Advanced Security or Code Security licence. The first job passes a public repository with an OSI licence, a caller that states the paid licence ( advanced_security: true ), or a private repository that the caller declares an open-source pre-release ( open_source_prerelease: true ): its code is under the OSI licence in its LICENSE file and is to be published. That declaration is the caller's responsibility; the job prints it as a warning and the report stays in the run's artifact. Anything else fails before CodeQL is downloaded. Caller ¶ jobs : misra : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-misra.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : level : safety cmake_args : "-DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON" cross_build_target : mychip_optimised_build cmake_args must build every translation unit that includes the code under paths . For a header-only driver, that is the host tests. The scan fails if a header under paths is not included by any translation unit. What it does ¶ Licence and configurations. The plan job checks the licence, then lists the configurations: host , and cortex-m unless cross: false . Deviation records. It reads the project-wide records ( compliance/misra-cpp-2023-deviations.yml of the handbook at handbook_ref ) and the repository's own MISRA records ( docs/deviations.yml , entries with check: misra/<guideline> ). Each record becomes one entry of the pack's deviation configuration. Its code identifier is the record id and its rule-id is the record's guideline. A lapsed record ( review_by passed) fails the scan. Traced build. It configures from scratch with compile_commands.json . The host uses g++ and the Cortex-M build uses arm-none-eabi-g++ with -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 . It then builds under codeql database create and compiles the canary into the same database. Analysis. It runs the pack's default suite, the profile pack and the pack's deviation suppression query, and writes the results as SARIF 2.1.0. Run-time assurance. The scan fails when any of these holds: a translation unit of the build is not in the database; a source file under paths is in no translation unit; the extractor reported an error; the canary's known violations were not all reported. Other tools on the same compile database. Build flags: it checks that every translation unit builds with the flags the compiler-decided guidelines rely on. clang-tidy: it runs each configuration the validation suite proved, mapped to its guidelines. cppcheck: it maps the message ids the matrix lists to guidelines. These are partial tools. Report. It merges the configurations into one report, with one row for each of the 179 guidelines. The report goes to the step summary, misra-summary.json (keyed by guideline), misra-findings.csv and one SARIF file per configuration, all in the misra-report artifact. The level's policy then decides whether the job fails. Deviations in the code ¶ A finding is deviated only by a marker that cites a record. The pack's forms are accepted: // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-004) return * reinterpret_cast < volatile std :: uint32_t *> ( address ); // codeql::misra_deviation(MD-CPP-003) A bare record id at the start or end of a comment also counts, so the NOLINT that MD-CPP-003 already asks for ( // NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-reinterpret-cast) MD-CPP-003 ) deviates the CodeQL finding as well. codeql::misra_deviation_begin(...) and codeql::misra_deviation_end(...) mark a range. Any of these is a suppression error , and fails the scan at every level: a marker citing an id that is no record; a marker for another standard ( codeql::autosar_deviation ); a marker that deviates no finding of its record's guideline in any configuration (a stale or misdirected marker); a NOLINT or cppcheck-suppress comment that cites no record id; a committed coding-standards.yml (deviations come from the records only). Levels ¶ Level Fails on high A finding of a mandatory or required guideline (our category) that no record deviates. Advisory findings are warnings safety Any finding no record deviates, and any translation unit built without the org flags ( -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wundef -Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti ) Both levels fail on suppression errors, a lapsed record, a missing canary detection or incomplete extraction. A rule the tool validation found reporting compliant code (a false positive in tests/misra-validation/anomalies.yml , for example a query that misreads code in class templates) does not decide its guideline alone. At the high level its findings are listed as to review in the summary and in misra-findings.csv (with the anomaly ids), and do not fail the job; the reviewer checks each one (review checklist R-FP), fixes a real one and needs no record for a false one. At the safety level they fail like any other finding. A recorded false negative never weakens a rule's findings. enforce: false reports only. The outputs carry the counts. A guideline without findings is reported as no findings , which proves nothing for an undecidable guideline. Those keep their review step (MISRA Compliance:2020 §3.5), as the plan explains. Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps plan (licence and configurations) contents: read actions/checkout ; actions/checkout ; Install PyYAML (pinned, hash-checked); May CodeQL run on this repository?; Configurations scan contents: read actions/checkout ; actions/checkout ; actions/checkout ; actions/cache ; Install the validated toolchain (toolchain.json, hash-checked); Tool versions; Scan; Upload the configuration's results report (per-guideline report) contents: read actions/checkout ; actions/checkout ; actions/download-artifact ; Install PyYAML (pinned, hash-checked); Report; Upload the report Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description level string high Failure policy. high: a finding of a mandatory or required guideline (our category) that no record deviates fails, an advisory one warns. safety: any finding that no record deviates fails, and every translation unit must build with the flags the compiler-decided guidelines rely on. paths string inc src Folders whose code is checked, space-separated, relative to the repository root cmake_source_dir string . Directory with the top-level CMakeLists.txt cmake_args string empty Configure arguments that build every translation unit of the code under paths (for example -DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON) build_target string empty Target of the host build; empty builds all cross boolean true Also analyse the Cortex-M build (cortex-m4f, the Arm GNU toolchain of toolchain.json), whose preprocessor paths differ from the host's cross_cmake_args string empty Configure arguments of the Cortex-M build; empty uses cmake_args cross_build_target string empty Target of the Cortex-M build (for example the driver's _optimised_build); empty builds all profile_pack boolean true Also run the Kokeb C++20 profile pack (codeql/kokeb-cpp20) of this workflow's commit repo_deviations string docs/deviations.yml The repository's own deviation records; entries with check: misra/ become code identifiers like the project-wide MD-CPP records handbook_ref string db2cdd0f75cdf998797d535565966b60e97f8c8d Commit of kokeb-labs/handbook whose compliance matrix and project-wide deviation records apply advanced_security boolean false Set true only if the organisation holds a paid GitHub Advanced Security or Code Security licence for this repository. Without it, CodeQL may run only on a public repository under an OSI-approved licence. open_source_prerelease boolean false Set true for a private repository whose code is released under the OSI-approved licence in its LICENSE file and is to be made public. CodeQL then runs and the job prints the declaration as a warning; the report stays in the run's artifact (nothing is uploaded to code scanning). enforce boolean true Fail the job by the level's policy. False reports only (the counts are in the outputs). artifact_name string misra-report Name of the report artifact (unique per call when a run calls this more than once) When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix "CodeQL may not run on a private repository" The repository is private, and neither advanced_security nor open_source_prerelease is set Make the repository public under its OSI licence, declare it an open-source pre-release, or hold the licence and set advanced_security: true "is under the analysed paths but no translation unit of this configuration includes it" A header is not built by cmake_args , or not by the cross target Build the host tests ( -D<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS=ON ) and a cross target that includes every header "the canary was not detected" The build was not traced, or a pack did not run Check the scan log; the build must run a real compiler, not a cache "suppression marker deviates no finding" The marker cites a record of another guideline, or the finding is gone Remove the marker, or cite the record of the finding's guideline "translation units build without -W..." (warning; error at safety ) The build does not use the org warning set Add the flags to the targets (the driver template's <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS ) A scan takes more than 20 minutes The CodeQL bundle and pack are downloaded The archives are cached by toolchain hash; the second run restores them Next: Tool validation plan

docs.text: ru-mkdocs-publish ¶ Build, check, audit and publish a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, versioned or not. ru-mkdocs-publish.yml builds a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, checks it, audits it and publishes it to gh-pages as a versioned site with mike , with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Migrating to MkDocs moves a repository onto it; the style guide says what its pages contain. Where the theme comes from ¶ The theme, the plugin, figkit and the pinned toolchain are the kokeb-mkdocs-theme package in packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme . Every job installs it with pip from the commit this workflow runs from (the job context's workflow_repository and workflow_sha ), so a caller pinned to @v1 builds with the theme released in v1 , and a branch under review builds with that branch's theme. theme_ref overrides the ref. A repository's own requirements-docs.txt , if it has one, is installed afterwards for extra plugins. What runs when ¶ Event Build + checks Lighthouse + screenshots Publish Pull request Yes Yes Never, whatever deploy says Push to the default branch Yes Yes Version dev (when deploy is true); dev also holds latest until the first release Push of a vX.Y.Z tag Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z ( release_version: minor : X.Y ), and latest moves to it Push of a vX.Y.Z-rc.N tag (any tag with - ) Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z-rc.N ; latest stays where it is With versioning: false (the organisation portal) there are no versions: see Unversioned sites . The site root redirects to latest . Aliases are symlinks, so the API reference added to a version folder is reachable through them too. Material's version selector in the header lists every version. Jobs and permissions ¶ The caller grants contents: write , even one that never publishes (pull requests, deploy: false ): GitHub checks the permissions of every job of a called workflow before the run starts, whatever the job's if . Job Permissions Steps build contents: read Check out (plus submodule_paths ), install the theme, run check_commands ( kokeb-docs check ), mkdocs build --strict , Doxygen into api/ (with the Kokeb Labs API stylesheet when the Doxyfile has none), lychee --offline --include-fragments on the merged site, upload docs-site quality contents: read Lighthouse CI (median of 3 runs, mobile emulation; the site served gzip-compressed as GitHub Pages serves it, by kokeb-docs serve ) on the home page and the first navigation pages against lighthouse_budgets , upload lighthouse-report ; Playwright screenshots at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark, upload docs-screenshots deploy contents: write Versioned: prune the pre-MkDocs site from gh-pages ( prune_legacy ), mike deploy , add the API reference to the version folder, mike set-default latest , root 404.html , push (never force). Unversioned: kokeb-docs publish-root commits the built site as the whole branch, push (never force) Every action is pinned to a commit SHA with its version in a comment. The first publish ¶ A repository with an older (Jekyll / Doxygen) site on gh-pages : everything at the top of the branch that is not a mike version or alias is removed in one commit before mike writes (kept: versions.json , index.html once mike owns it, 404.html , .nojekyll , CNAME , robots.txt ). A repository without gh-pages : mike creates the branch. In both cases the root gets mike's redirect to latest/ and a 404.html that sends old addresses to the same page under latest/ ( /docs/x/ , /development/x/ to latest/x/ ; /doxs/ , /html/ to latest/api/ ). Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description python_version string 3.12 Python used to build the site. requirements string requirements-docs.txt Optional pip requirements file installed after the theme package (extra MkDocs plugins). Skipped when the file does not exist; the theme package already pins mkdocs, mkdocs-material, awesome-nav, pymdown and mike. theme_ref string empty Ref of kokeb-labs/ci-tools to install the theme package from. Empty: the commit this workflow runs from, so the theme always matches the workflow. mkdocs_config string mkdocs.yml Path of the site configuration. A repository that keeps tool configuration out of its root passes _config/mkdocs.yml (with docs_dir: ../docs); the theme then takes the folder that holds docs_dir as the repository root (snippets, repository links, figures) and the check commands get it as KOKEB_DOCS_CONFIG. submodules string false Submodules to check out with the repository: 'false', 'true' (top level) or 'recursive'. submodule_paths string empty Space-separated submodule paths to initialise (shallow) after checkout, nested ones included: each parent submodule on the way is initialised without recursion, e.g. 'lib/core/drivers/internal/pincfg'. Use it instead of 'recursive' when the checks need a few nested submodules. check_commands string if [ -f tools/figkit/build.py ]; then python3 tools/figkit/build.py --check; fi if [ -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then python3 tools/docs/gen.py --check; fi if [ ! -f tools/figkit/build.py ] && [ ! -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then kokeb-docs check; fi Shell lines run before the build, with GH_TOKEN set to the job's read-only token (for commands that read the GitHub API); any failure fails the job. The default runs the figure drift check and the generated-region check (kokeb-docs check), or a repository's own tools/figkit and tools/docs/gen.py when it still carries them. doxygen_config string empty Doxyfile for the API reference, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: no API. doxygen_working_directory string . Directory Doxygen runs in; relative paths in the Doxyfile resolve against it. doxygen_html_dir string empty Directory of the generated HTML, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: read OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and HTML_OUTPUT from the Doxyfile. api_dir string api Folder of the site that receives the Doxygen HTML (match extra.api_dir in mkdocs.yml). link_check boolean true Run lychee offline on the built site (internal links, anchors and images, API included). link_check_args string empty Extra lychee arguments, for example --exclude-path patterns. lighthouse boolean true Run Lighthouse on the built site (home page and the first navigation pages) against the budgets. lighthouse_budgets string performance=0.8 accessibility=0.95 best-practices=0.9 seo=0.9 Minimum Lighthouse category scores (0-1, median of three runs, mobile emulation), space-separated category=score pairs. A score below its minimum fails the job. screenshots boolean true Capture the home page and the first navigation pages at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark (artifact). versioning boolean true true: a versioned site, published with mike (default branch -> dev_version, v* tag -> that version, with latest_alias moved to it). false: one unversioned site (the organisation portal), published from the default branch as the whole content of deployment_branch at its root (a custom domain only from a CNAME file in the site); tags publish nothing. The build tells the theme plugin which (KOKEB_DOCS_VERSIONED), so site_url and the version selector match. deploy boolean false Publish to deployment_branch. Never happens on a pull_request event, whatever this says; callers usually pass a repository-variable gate here. deployment_branch string gh-pages Branch GitHub Pages serves from. dev_version string dev mike version name a push to the default branch publishes to. latest_alias string latest mike alias moved to each release (v* tag). release_version string tag Version name a v* tag publishes: 'tag' (the tag itself, vX.Y.Z) or 'minor' (X.Y, a patch release replaces the docs of its minor release). prune_legacy boolean true On publish, remove every top-level entry of the deployment branch that is not a mike version or alias (the old Jekyll / Doxygen site: development/, doxs/, html/, version_selector.html, ...), in the publish commit. Kept: versions.json, index.html, 404.html, .nojekyll, CNAME, robots.txt. Example ¶ name : 📚 Docs on : push : branches : [ main ] tags : [ 'v*' ] pull_request : branches : [ main ] permissions : contents : read concurrency : group : docs-${{ github.ref }} cancel-in-progress : ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} jobs : docs : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-mkdocs-publish.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : doxygen_config : Doxyfile deploy : true Configuration in _config/ ¶ A repository whose root holds only what GitHub and readers look for keeps the site configuration in _config/ with docs_dir: ../docs and passes its path: with : mkdocs_config : _config/mkdocs.yml doxygen_config : _config/Doxyfile The build, the drift checks ( KOKEB_DOCS_CONFIG is set from mkdocs_config ), the pip cache key and mike all use that path, and the theme takes the folder that holds docs_dir as the repository root, so snippets and repository links are unchanged. Doxygen runs in doxygen_working_directory (default the root), so paths inside a _config/Doxyfile stay relative to the root. Unversioned sites ¶ The organisation portal ( kokeb-labs.github.io ) has one current site, not versions. With versioning: false : Piece Versioned (default) Unversioned site_url https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/latest/ https://kokeb-labs.github.io/ (or /<repo>/ ) Version selector, older-version banner Yes No Push to the default branch Publishes dev Replaces the whole deployment branch with the built site, in one ordinary commit ( .nojekyll written; a CNAME only when the site has one, docs/CNAME ; no commit when nothing changed) Push of a v* tag Publishes vX.Y.Z Nothing (a notice) Pull request Build, checks, Lighthouse, screenshots The same The build job tells the theme plugin through KOKEB_DOCS_VERSIONED , so the input decides both the build and the publish. A local build of the portal needs nothing: the plugin treats <org>.github.io as unversioned on its own, and plugins: [{kokeb: {versioned: false}}] does the same for any other site. jobs : site : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-mkdocs-publish.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : versioning : false deploy : true Pages must serve the gh-pages branch from / once the first publish has run; until then, leave the Pages source as it is, so the current site stays up. After the first publish ¶ GitHub Pages must serve the gh-pages branch from / ( Settings > Pages > Build and deployment : source Deploy from a branch , branch gh-pages , folder / ). The workflow never changes repository settings. docs.text: Build, check, audit and publish a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, versioned or not. ru-mkdocs-publish.yml builds a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, checks it, audits it and publishes it to gh-pages as a versioned site with mike , with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Migrating to MkDocs moves a repository onto it; the style guide says what its pages contain.
docs.title: ru-mkdocs-publish

docs.text: The theme, the plugin, figkit and the pinned toolchain are the kokeb-mkdocs-theme package in packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme . Every job installs it with pip from the commit this workflow runs from (the job context's workflow_repository and workflow_sha ), so a caller pinned to @v1 builds with the theme released in v1 , and a branch under review builds with that branch's theme. theme_ref overrides the ref. A repository's own requirements-docs.txt , if it has one, is installed afterwards for extra plugins.
docs.title: Where the theme comes from

docs.text: Event Build + checks Lighthouse + screenshots Publish Pull request Yes Yes Never, whatever deploy says Push to the default branch Yes Yes Version dev (when deploy is true); dev also holds latest until the first release Push of a vX.Y.Z tag Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z ( release_version: minor : X.Y ), and latest moves to it Push of a vX.Y.Z-rc.N tag (any tag with - ) Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z-rc.N ; latest stays where it is With versioning: false (the organisation portal) there are no versions: see Unversioned sites . The site root redirects to latest . Aliases are symlinks, so the API reference added to a version folder is reachable through them too. Material's version selector in the header lists every version.
docs.title: What runs when

docs.text: The caller grants contents: write , even one that never publishes (pull requests, deploy: false ): GitHub checks the permissions of every job of a called workflow before the run starts, whatever the job's if . Job Permissions Steps build contents: read Check out (plus submodule_paths ), install the theme, run check_commands ( kokeb-docs check ), mkdocs build --strict , Doxygen into api/ (with the Kokeb Labs API stylesheet when the Doxyfile has none), lychee --offline --include-fragments on the merged site, upload docs-site quality contents: read Lighthouse CI (median of 3 runs, mobile emulation; the site served gzip-compressed as GitHub Pages serves it, by kokeb-docs serve ) on the home page and the first navigation pages against lighthouse_budgets , upload lighthouse-report ; Playwright screenshots at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark, upload docs-screenshots deploy contents: write Versioned: prune the pre-MkDocs site from gh-pages ( prune_legacy ), mike deploy , add the API reference to the version folder, mike set-default latest , root 404.html , push (never force). Unversioned: kokeb-docs publish-root commits the built site as the whole branch, push (never force) Every action is pinned to a commit SHA with its version in a comment.
docs.title: Jobs and permissions

docs.text: A repository with an older (Jekyll / Doxygen) site on gh-pages : everything at the top of the branch that is not a mike version or alias is removed in one commit before mike writes (kept: versions.json , index.html once mike owns it, 404.html , .nojekyll , CNAME , robots.txt ). A repository without gh-pages : mike creates the branch. In both cases the root gets mike's redirect to latest/ and a 404.html that sends old addresses to the same page under latest/ ( /docs/x/ , /development/x/ to latest/x/ ; /doxs/ , /html/ to latest/api/ ).

docs.text: Input Type Default Description python_version string 3.12 Python used to build the site. requirements string requirements-docs.txt Optional pip requirements file installed after the theme package (extra MkDocs plugins). Skipped when the file does not exist; the theme package already pins mkdocs, mkdocs-material, awesome-nav, pymdown and mike. theme_ref string empty Ref of kokeb-labs/ci-tools to install the theme package from. Empty: the commit this workflow runs from, so the theme always matches the workflow. mkdocs_config string mkdocs.yml Path of the site configuration. A repository that keeps tool configuration out of its root passes _config/mkdocs.yml (with docs_dir: ../docs); the theme then takes the folder that holds docs_dir as the repository root (snippets, repository links, figures) and the check commands get it as KOKEB_DOCS_CONFIG. submodules string false Submodules to check out with the repository: 'false', 'true' (top level) or 'recursive'. submodule_paths string empty Space-separated submodule paths to initialise (shallow) after checkout, nested ones included: each parent submodule on the way is initialised without recursion, e.g. 'lib/core/drivers/internal/pincfg'. Use it instead of 'recursive' when the checks need a few nested submodules. check_commands string if [ -f tools/figkit/build.py ]; then python3 tools/figkit/build.py --check; fi if [ -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then python3 tools/docs/gen.py --check; fi if [ ! -f tools/figkit/build.py ] && [ ! -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then kokeb-docs check; fi Shell lines run before the build, with GH_TOKEN set to the job's read-only token (for commands that read the GitHub API); any failure fails the job. The default runs the figure drift check and the generated-region check (kokeb-docs check), or a repository's own tools/figkit and tools/docs/gen.py when it still carries them. doxygen_config string empty Doxyfile for the API reference, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: no API. doxygen_working_directory string . Directory Doxygen runs in; relative paths in the Doxyfile resolve against it. doxygen_html_dir string empty Directory of the generated HTML, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: read OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and HTML_OUTPUT from the Doxyfile. api_dir string api Folder of the site that receives the Doxygen HTML (match extra.api_dir in mkdocs.yml). link_check boolean true Run lychee offline on the built site (internal links, anchors and images, API included). link_check_args string empty Extra lychee arguments, for example --exclude-path patterns. lighthouse boolean true Run Lighthouse on the built site (home page and the first navigation pages) against the budgets. lighthouse_budgets string performance=0.8 accessibility=0.95 best-practices=0.9 seo=0.9 Minimum Lighthouse category scores (0-1, median of three runs, mobile emulation), space-separated category=score pairs. A score below its minimum fails the job. screenshots boolean true Capture the home page and the first navigation pages at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark (artifact). versioning boolean true true: a versioned site, published with mike (default branch -> dev_version, v* tag -> that version, with latest_alias moved to it). false: one unversioned site (the organisation portal), published from the default branch as the whole content of deployment_branch at its root (a custom domain only from a CNAME file in the site); tags publish nothing. The build tells the theme plugin which (KOKEB_DOCS_VERSIONED), so site_url and the version selector match. deploy boolean false Publish to deployment_branch. Never happens on a pull_request event, whatever this says; callers usually pass a repository-variable gate here. deployment_branch string gh-pages Branch GitHub Pages serves from. dev_version string dev mike version name a push to the default branch publishes to. latest_alias string latest mike alias moved to each release (v* tag). release_version string tag Version name a v* tag publishes: 'tag' (the tag itself, vX.Y.Z) or 'minor' (X.Y, a patch release replaces the docs of its minor release). prune_legacy boolean true On publish, remove every top-level entry of the deployment branch that is not a mike version or alias (the old Jekyll / Doxygen site: development/, doxs/, html/, version_selector.html, ...), in the publish commit. Kept: versions.json, index.html, 404.html, .nojekyll, CNAME, robots.txt.

docs.text: ru-release-firmware ¶ Create a GitHub Release for a tag and attach the firmware that ru-build built and tested for the same commit, in public and private repositories. File: .github/workflows/ru-release-firmware.yml It replaces ru-release-with-artifacts , with the same inputs and behaviour. The difference is one permission: its job asks for actions: read as well as contents: write , so it can find the tagged commit's CI run in a private repository. Caller ¶ --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-firmware.yml@v1 permissions : actions : read contents : write with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml fail_on_no_artifacts : true Grant both permissions. A caller that grants only contents: write gets startup_failure . Release only after CI passed on the tag ¶ Triggered by the tag push itself, the release runs at the same time as CI on that tag and can publish before (or without) a green build. Trigger it from the finished CI run instead, and pass the tag and the commit: on : workflow_run : workflows : [ CI ] types : [ completed ] permissions : actions : read contents : write jobs : release : if : >- github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' && startsWith(github.event.workflow_run.head_branch, 'v') uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-firmware.yml@v1 with : build_workflow : ci.yml tag_name : ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }} commit : ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }} fail_on_no_artifacts : true The workflow checks that the tag points to commit before it releases anything. Move from ru-release-with-artifacts ¶ Change two lines in the calling workflow: the file name in uses: , and actions: read next to contents: write in its permissions. The inputs are the same, so with: stays as it is. jobs : release : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-firmware.yml@v1 # was ru-release-with-artifacts.yml permissions : actions : read # new contents : write Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description build_workflow string esp32-examples-build-ci.yml Name of the ESP32 build workflow artifact_pattern string fw-.* Pattern for firmware artifacts draft boolean false Create as draft release prerelease boolean false Mark as pre-release tag_name string empty Tag name for release (defaults to github.ref_name) fail_on_no_artifacts boolean false Fail if no firmware artifacts found commit string empty Commit whose CI artifacts are released, and that the release tag must point to. Empty: github.sha. A caller triggered by workflow_run passes github.event.workflow_run.head_sha, because github.sha is then the default branch's head, not the tagged commit. Jobs and permissions ¶ One job, release , with actions: read and contents: write . It checks out with full history, downloads every artifact whose name matches artifact_pattern from the run of build_workflow on commit (default github.sha ) ( dawidd6/action-download-artifact ), builds the release files with tools/release_assets/release_assets.py from ci-tools at the same commit as this workflow, and creates the release for tag_name (default: the pushed tag) with generated notes and those files attached ( softprops/action-gh-release ). The checksums also go to the run's summary. Permission What needs it contents: write Creating the release and uploading its files actions: read Listing the build workflow's runs to find the tagged commit's run, and downloading its artifacts. A public repository allows both reads without it; a private one refuses them with Resource not accessible by integration What the release holds ¶ For tag v1.2.0 of a repository whose driver.yml names it as5047u : File What it is as5047u-1.2.0.tar.gz The tagged tree ( git archive ), compressed with a fixed date: the same tag always gives the same bytes. GitHub's own "Source code" archives are not promised to be byte-stable, so checksums name this one. Submodules are not inside; the SBOM names each at its pinned commit. as5047u-1.2.0.spdx.json SBOM, SPDX 2.3 JSON: the repository as the main package (licence from LICENSE , the archive's SHA-256, the tagged commit), each git submodule as a package it contains (URL and pinned commit), and each firmware zip as a file generated from it. fw-<app>-<idf>-<type>.zip One per firmware artifact: for each ESP-IDF build in it, flasher_args.json , flash_args , every file they flash (bootloader, partition table, app) and the app's .elf and .map , at their build paths. An artifact with no flasher_args.json is zipped whole, with a warning. SHA256SUMS SHA-256 of every other file, in sha256sum -c format. One zip per artifact keeps Debug and Release apart. Uploading the build folders file by file, as versions before 1.7.0 did, attached thousands of files (an ESP-IDF build folder holds about 1,500), let files with the same name in Debug and Release overwrite each other, and could pass GitHub's limit of 1,000 files per release. Check a download ¶ gh release download v1.2.0 -R kokeb-labs/driver-as5047u -D v1.2.0 cd v1.2.0 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS Every line must say OK . To flash a firmware zip: unzip it, go to the build folder inside and run esptool.py --chip <chip> write_flash @flash_args (the chip is in flasher_args.json ). Provenance ¶ For a public repository, add ru-attest-release as a job after this one. It signs build provenance for every file in SHA256SUMS , and gh attestation verify checks a download against it. It is a separate workflow because it needs id-token: write and attestations: write , which callers of this workflow do not grant. When it finds no firmware ¶ The release only reuses artifacts; it never builds. It finds none when: the build workflow has not run on the tagged commit (tag a commit that was pushed to a branch the build runs on, and wait for that build to finish); the artifacts expired ( ru-build keeps them 7 days); build_workflow names a different file than the caller of ru-build ; artifact_pattern (a regular expression, default fw-.* ) does not match. With fail_on_no_artifacts: false (the default) the release is still created, without firmware, and the step logs a warning. Set it to true to fail instead. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure The calling job does not grant contents: write and actions: read Grant both in the calling job, or at the top of the calling workflow Resource not accessible by integration - .../rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow in the download step The token cannot read workflow runs: the caller still calls ru-release-with-artifacts , or the repository restricts the workflow token Call this workflow with actions: read granted; check Settings > Actions > Workflow permissions Resource not accessible by integration when creating the release The repository restricts the workflow token to read Grant contents: write in the caller; check Settings > Actions > Workflow permissions Release has no firmware zips See above Set fail_on_no_artifacts: true to catch it release files share a name Two artifacts would give zips with the same name Give the artifacts distinct names ( ru-build names them by app, IDF version and build type) flasher_args.json lists files the artifact lacks The build artifact was uploaded without part of the build Upload the whole build folder in ru-build tag ... points to ..., not to the released commit The tag names another commit than commit (default github.sha ) Pass the tagged commit as commit , or tag the commit CI built tag ... does not exist here The release ran for a tag that was not pushed Push the tag first Next: ensure-tools-directory , for your own jobs that need the project tools.

Empty: github.sha. A caller triggered by workflow_run passes github.event.workflow_run.head_sha, because github.sha is then the default branch's head, not the tagged commit. Jobs and permissions ¶ One job, release , with contents: write . It checks out with full history, downloads every artifact whose name matches artifact_pattern from the run of build_workflow on github.sha ( dawidd6/action-download-artifact ), builds the release files with tools/release_assets/release_assets.py from ci-tools at the same commit as this workflow, and creates the release for tag_name (default: the pushed tag) with generated notes and those files attached ( softprops/action-gh-release ). The checksums also go to the run's summary. The workflow does not ask for actions: read , because existing callers grant only contents: write and would hit startup_failure . Without it the token can list workflow runs and download their artifacts only in a public repository. A private repository refuses those reads with Resource not accessible by integration ; use ru-release-firmware there. What the release holds ¶ For tag v1.2.0 of a repository whose driver.yml names it as5047u : File What it is as5047u-1.2.0.tar.gz The tagged tree ( git archive ), compressed with a fixed date: the same tag always gives the same bytes. GitHub's own "Source code" archives are not promised to be byte-stable, so checksums name this one. Submodules are not inside; the SBOM names each at its pinned commit. as5047u-1.2.0.spdx.json SBOM, SPDX 2.3 JSON: the repository as the main package (licence from LICENSE , the archive's SHA-256, the tagged commit), each git submodule as a package it contains (URL and pinned commit), and each firmware zip as a file generated from it. fw-<app>-<idf>-<type>.zip One per firmware artifact: for each ESP-IDF build in it, flasher_args.json , flash_args , every file they flash (bootloader, partition table, app) and the app's .elf and .map , at their build paths. An artifact with no flasher_args.json is zipped whole, with a warning. SHA256SUMS SHA-256 of every other file, in sha256sum -c format. One zip per artifact keeps Debug and Release apart. Uploading the build folders file by file, as versions before 1.7.0 did, attached thousands of files (an ESP-IDF build folder holds about 1,500), let files with the same name in Debug and Release overwrite each other, and could pass GitHub's limit of 1,000 files per release. Check a download ¶ gh release download v1.2.0 -R kokeb-labs/driver-as5047u -D v1.2.0 cd v1.2.0 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS Every line must say OK . To flash a firmware zip: unzip it, go to the build folder inside and run esptool.py --chip <chip> write_flash @flash_args (the chip is in flasher_args.json ). Provenance ¶ For a public repository, add ru-attest-release as a job after this one. It signs build provenance for every file in SHA256SUMS , and gh attestation verify checks a download against it. It is a separate workflow because it needs id-token: write and attestations: write , which callers of this workflow do not grant. When it finds no firmware ¶ The release only reuses artifacts; it never builds. It finds none when: the build workflow has not run on the tagged commit (tag a commit that was pushed to a branch the build runs on, and wait for that build to finish); the artifacts expired ( ru-build keeps them 7 days); build_workflow names a different file than the caller of ru-build ; artifact_pattern (a regular expression, default fw-.* ) does not match. With fail_on_no_artifacts: false (the default) the release is still created, without firmware, and the step logs a warning. Set it to true to fail instead. docs.text: ru-repo-checks ¶ The small checks of a repository (sign-off, organisation standard, Markdown and YAML lint, handbook rules, template drift and cppcheck) as steps of one job, with the same scripts and failure rules as their single workflows. GitHub bills every job of a private repository rounded up to a whole minute. Each of these checks takes 5 to 15 seconds, so as seven jobs they cost seven minutes a run; as one job they cost one or two. Step Same as Fails the job when Turn off DCO dco a commit of the pull request has no Signed-off-by matching its author run_dco: false Org standard org-standard-check a required root file is missing or empty, or LICENSE is not MIT run_org_standard: false Markdown lint ru-markdown-lint (the markdownlint-cli2 action) markdownlint reports an issue run_markdown_lint: false Handbook rules ru-handbook-check a handbook error (with handbook_enforce: true , the default) run_handbook: false Template drift ru-template-drift never by default; with template_drift_enforce: true , on drift run_template_drift: false cppcheck ru-cpp-analysis cppcheck itself fails, or with cppcheck_strict: true it reports a finding run_cppcheck: false YAML lint ru-yaml-lint yamllint reports an error (with yaml_strict_mode: true , a warning too) run_yaml_lint: false Every check runs whether or not an earlier one failed, and writes the summary its single workflow writes. The job summary ends with one line per check, and the failed output lists the checks that failed. The self-CI ( check_repo_checks.py ) fails when a step here differs from the step of the single workflow it copies, so a fix to one reaches the other. Caller ¶ jobs : checks : name : Repository checks uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-repo-checks.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : read with : markdown_globs : 'docs/** *.md **/*.md' cppcheck_paths : "inc src" cppcheck_strict : true Add the job to the CI gate's needs . DCO passes with nothing to check on an event that is not a pull request (a push to main , a tag), so the job always runs and needs no allow_skipped entry, unlike a dco.yml job that is skipped outside pull requests. Order and trust ¶ DCO first , before anything is checked out. It reads the commits through the API, so no code of the pull request has run in the job when the verdict is made. The caller's checkout, then the organisation standard and the Markdown lint. The handbook checker (this repository's tools/handbook_check at the workflow's own commit) and driver-template (for its scaffold.py --check-drift ) are checked out into the workspace, after the Markdown lint so that they are never linted as the caller's files. They are removed again before the YAML lint. cppcheck, then the YAML lint last: its install puts yamllint's virtual environment on PATH . The job has contents: read and pull-requests: read only, no secrets and no cache, so nothing it runs can write to the caller's repository, its pull requests, its caches or its releases. Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps checks (repository checks) contents: read , pull-requests: read DCO: check the sign-off of every commit; actions/checkout ; Org standard: required files and the MIT licence; Markdown lint: markdownlint-cli2; Markdown lint: result; Handbook: check out the checker; Handbook: install PyYAML (pinned, hash-checked); Handbook: check; Template drift: check out driver-template; Template drift: compare with the template; cppcheck: install; cppcheck: run; cppcheck: upload the report; cppcheck: fail on findings (strict); Remove the checked-out tools; YAML lint: install yamllint (pinned, hash-checked); YAML lint: yamllint; Summary Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description run_dco boolean true Run the DCO sign-off check (pull requests; on other events it passes with nothing to check) dco_allow_bots boolean true Accept commits whose GitHub author is a bot account (type Bot, or a login ending in [bot]), such as Dependabot or github-actions, without a sign-off. dco_skip_merge_commits boolean true Accept merge commits (more than one parent) without a sign-off; they add no authored change of their own. run_org_standard boolean true Run the organisation-standard check (required root files, MIT licence) org_standard_extra_files string empty More files that must exist, as paths relative to the repository root separated by spaces or newlines (for example SECURITY.md docs/index.md ). The organisation's own list is always checked. run_markdown_lint boolean true Run markdownlint-cli2 markdown_globs string **/*.md Space-separated glob patterns of the Markdown files to check markdown_config_file string _config/.markdownlint.json Path of the markdownlint configuration file markdown_fix boolean false Fix fixable issues (markdownlint --fix); the runner's fix is not committed markdown_separator string empty Separator between the glob patterns. Empty: a space. run_handbook boolean true Run the handbook check handbook_path string . Directory of the repository the handbook check reads, relative to the checkout root handbook_enforce boolean true Fail on a handbook error. False reports only (the counts are in the outputs). run_template_drift boolean true Run the template drift check (a repository without .kokeb/template.yml gets a warning) template_drift_ref string main Branch, tag or commit of kokeb-labs/driver-template to compare against template_drift_enforce boolean false Fail on template drift. False reports only, as warnings on the drifted files. run_cppcheck boolean true Run cppcheck cppcheck_paths string src inc examples Directories cppcheck analyses (space-separated) cppcheck_std string c++20 C++ standard cppcheck_strict boolean false Fail when cppcheck reports a finding (severity other than information) cppcheck_exclude string empty Paths cppcheck leaves out (space-separated) cppcheck_enable string warning,style,performance,portability,information Checks to enable (comma-separated: all,warning,style,performance, portability,information,unusedFunction,missingInclude) cppcheck_force boolean false Force checking even with incomplete analysis cppcheck_max_configs number 0 Maximum configs to check (for template-heavy code, 0=unlimited) cppcheck_artifact_name string cppcheck-report Name of the uploaded cppcheck report artifact (unique per call when a run calls this more than once) run_yaml_lint boolean true Run yamllint yaml_paths string **/*.yml,**/*.yaml Comma-separated paths or glob patterns of the YAML files to check yaml_config_file string _config/.yamllint Path of the yamllint configuration file yaml_strict_mode boolean false Fail on yamllint warnings too (--strict) yaml_exclude_patterns string .git/**,node_modules/**,venv/**,.venv/**,**/espidf-tools/** Comma-separated patterns of files the YAML lint leaves out

docs.text: ru-template-drift ¶ Find the files a driver or library has let drift from driver-template . Every scaffolded repository keeps a copy of the template's shell: the CI workflows, the tool configuration in _config/ , the agent skills and the CMake helpers. A fix in the template does not reach those copies by itself. ru-template-drift.yml scaffolds the template again with the arguments the repository was made with ( .kokeb/template.yml , written by the scaffold) and compares each file the template manages. Code, tests, docs, the README, the changelog and _config/Kconfig are the repository's own and are never compared. The comparison is the template's own tools/scaffold.py --check-drift , so it always knows what the template makes today. With enforce: true drift fails the job. docs.text: Find the files a driver or library has let drift from driver-template . Every scaffolded repository keeps a copy of the template's shell: the CI workflows, the tool configuration in _config/ , the agent skills and the CMake helpers. A fix in the template does not reach those copies by itself. ru-template-drift.yml scaffolds the template again with the arguments the repository was made with ( .kokeb/template.yml , written by the scaffold) and compares each file the template manages. Code, tests, docs, the README, the changelog and _config/Kconfig are the repository's own and are never compared. The comparison is the template's own tools/scaffold.py --check-drift , so it always knows what the template makes today.

docs.text: ru-yaml-lint ¶ Lint YAML files with yamllint against the repository's own rules. ru-yaml-lint.yml installs yamllint and runs it on every file matched by paths (comma-separated globs) that is not excluded by exclude_patterns , with config_file when it exists (yamllint's defaults otherwise). What it does ¶ Expands each glob in paths (with ** ), or finds matching files when the glob matches nothing. Drops files whose path contains one of exclude_patterns . Runs yamllint on each file, with --strict when strict_mode is set, so warnings fail too. Fails when any file has errors (or warnings, in strict mode). Outputs: result , files_checked , issues_found . docs.text: Trigger policy ¶ Which events may start a workflow in this repository and in the repositories made from the templates, and why. The rule ¶ A workflow starts only from: Trigger Runs in the context of push The pushed branch or tag pull_request The pull request's merge ref, with a read-only token for forks merge_group The merge queue's temporary branch workflow_call The caller's event: one of the rows above release.yml is the one exception: it starts from workflow_run when the self-CI finishes on main , and checks out only the commit that self-CI tested. Not allowed: workflow_dispatch , schedule , pull_request_target , issue_comment , workflow_run (outside release.yml ) and the other events that run in the default branch's context. To run a workflow again, use Re-run jobs on its run; to run it on a branch, push the branch or open a draft pull request. The self-CI enforces the rule: .github/scripts/check_triggers.py fails on any other trigger in .github/workflows/ or in a template's workflows. Why ¶ A run started by one of those events executes in the context of the default branch. It can write the Actions cache entries that every later run on main , and every release built from main , restores. If such a run executes code it checked out by a computed ref, that code could leave a poisoned cache entry behind ( CodeQL actions/cache-poisoning/poisonable-step ). Several workflows here must run code checked out by a computed ref: the handbook checker and the template drift check run ci-tools' own scripts at the commit of the workflow ( job.workflow_sha ), and template drift runs driver-template's scaffold at the caller's recorded version. Those refs are trusted, but neither CodeQL nor a reviewer can tell that from the expression alone. Removing the privileged triggers removes the risk instead of explaining it away: no run of these workflows can write the default branch's cache from code that a pull request chose. A manual trigger bought nothing a re-run does not give: every check already runs on each push and pull request. For callers ¶ Repositories made from driver-template follow the same rule: their workflow files have no workflow_dispatch either. An ESP-IDF clean build needs no manual input: the caches are keyed by IDF commit and source, and gh cache delete --all empties them when a clean build is wanted. Code scanning: untrusted checkout ¶ Code scanning runs security-and-quality , which includes actions/untrusted-checkout/medium . That query reports every actions/checkout whose ref: names a ref, SHA or head in a workflow a pull request can start; it cannot tell a pinned ci-tools or handbook commit from a pull request's branch. Every reusable workflow here checks out that way by design, and what the query warns about (a self-hosted runner, a cache or artifact that a privileged workflow later trusts) is ruled out by this trigger policy, GitHub-hosted runners, read-only tokens and persist-credentials: false . .github/codeql/codeql-config.yml therefore excludes the medium variant, with this reasoning, and keeps actions/untrusted-checkout/high (privileged triggers), which reports any regression.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. From push to release ¶ From push to release Figure description and sources Two lanes, each read left to right. The top lane runs on every push and pull request: the caller's esp32-examples-build-ci.yml calls ru-build, whose generate-matrix job checks out espidf-tools and turns app_config.yml into a matrix, whose build job runs once per matrix entry in the espressif/idf image, and whose size-report job comments a size table on pull requests. The build job uploads one fw-* artifact per entry. The bottom lane runs when a version tag is pushed: the caller's release.yml calls ru-release-firmware, which downloads those artifacts for the tagged commit and attaches them to a GitHub Release, so nothing is rebuilt. Solid arrows mean "runs next", dashed arrows carry files. Job names are read from the workflow files. docs.text: Tool validation plan ¶ How the static-analysis toolchain behind the MISRA C++:2023 compliance matrix is validated for use under the quality management system of an IEC 62304 Class C product, and how the evidence stays current. Purpose and scope ¶ The compliance matrix says, guideline by guideline, which tool decides it. A tool that decides a guideline replaces a reviewer for that guideline. If the tool misses a violation, nobody else is looking. Every such claim therefore needs evidence that the tool, in our configuration, does what the matrix says. This plan defines that evidence: its requirements, test cases, acceptance criteria, records and re-validation. In scope are the tools whose output is verification evidence for C++ code in drivers, libraries, HALs and firmware: compiler warnings clang-tidy cppcheck the CodeQL MISRA C++:2023 pack and our own C++20 profile pack the handbook checks the scripts of ru-misra that run them Compilers as code generators, debuggers and the documentation tools are out of scope. Governing expectations ¶ Source What it asks of us How this plan meets it ISO 13485:2016 §4.1.6, §7.5.6 (and §7.6) Documented procedures to validate software used in the QMS, before first use and after changes, with effort proportionate to the risk of its use, and records This plan; the suite in the repository; the record re-made on every change; re-validation enforced by the self-CI ISO/TR 80002-2:2017 Critical thinking, intended use first, risk-driven choice of confidence-building activities, a validation plan and report, maintenance and change control Intended use per tool; scripted tests chosen by classification; the report per release; change control through the record check FDA, Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software (final, 3 February 2026) Risk-based assurance: scripted testing where process risk is high; records of intended use, risk, tests, issues and conclusion Process risk is high (a missed violation in Class C code), so every claim is tested by script and recorded; anomalies are logged with dispositions FDA, General Principles of Software Validation (2002), §5.2.4, §5.2.5 The most rigorous compiler error checking for the final build, warnings documented; test tools of a quality no less than the product they test -Werror with the org warning set is checked in every translation unit; this validation IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015, 5.1.4, 5.1.10, 5.1.12, 8.1 Plan development tools; control supporting items such as tools and their settings; identify the defect categories of the language and show they do not lead to unacceptable risk; identify configuration items and versions The toolchain is a controlled supporting item ( tools/misra/toolchain.json , versions and hashes in the record). The matrix plus this validation are the evidence for 5.1.12. IEC 62304 has no tool-qualification clause of its own, so tool validation follows from ISO 13485 §4.1.6 ISO 26262-8:2018 clause 11 Classify tools by tool impact (TI) and tool error detection (TD) into a tool confidence level (TCL); qualify TCL2/TCL3 tools, for example by validation of the software tool (11.4.9) Used as a recognised method for the classification ; qualification by validation (method 1c) MISRA Compliance:2020 §2.6.2–§2.6.5, §3.3–§3.5 Justify trust in analysers and compilers; a test suite of violations; validate with the product's options and libraries; keep a known-defects list; know which guidelines each tool checks; a guideline enforcement plan with tool versions and configuration; investigate every message; no finding is not proof for undecidable guidelines The suite seeds violations per guideline; it is compiled with the product's flags and libraries; the anomaly log is the known-defects list; the matrix is the guideline enforcement plan; undecidable guidelines keep review Sources: - ISO 13485:2016, reading copy - ISO/TR 80002-2:2017, public sample - FDA CSA guidance - FDA General Principles of Software Validation ; its section 6 is superseded by CSA - IEC 62304 AMD1, public sample - ISO 26262-8 clause 11, public summary - MISRA Compliance:2020 The table paraphrases these sources. The licensed standards themselves are held by the maintainer. Intended use and confidence classification ¶ Tool impact is TI2 for every tool here: each can fail to report a violation it is relied on to find. The tool error detection (TD) column says how likely a tool error is to be caught later in our process. The method is ISO 26262-8 Table 3: TI2 with TD1 gives TCL1, with TD2 gives TCL2, with TD3 gives TCL3. Tool Intended use TD and reasoning TCL Confidence from GCC and Clang warnings, -Werror Decide the guidelines the matrix assigns to a warning option, or to a hard error (exceptions, RTTI, preprocessor). TD2: the warnings are front-end checks on syntax, and the CodeQL queries cover most of the same guidelines independently. TCL2 Validation of the tool (suite, every claim, GCC 14, Clang 18, Arm GNU 14.3); confidence from use clang-tidy 20.1.0 Decide the guidelines the matrix assigns to a check, with the CheckOptions the suite records. TD2: most of these guidelines also have a CodeQL query. TCL2 Validation of the tool (suite); confidence from use CodeQL 2.21.4 with codeql/misra-cpp-coding-standards 2.62.0 Report violations of 175 guidelines. This decides the decidable translation-unit guidelines whose queries the suite proves, and is partial for the undecidable and system-scope ones. TD3 for guidelines where it would be the only tool. The pack's own validation covers C++14/17 with gcc 8.4, clang 10 and qcc 8.3 only, not our C++20 and compilers. TCL3 Validation of the tool (suite with true positives, true negatives and near misses, both configurations); the vendor's test suite and qualification material for their configurations; the anomaly log Kokeb C++20 profile pack ( codeql/kokeb-cpp20 ) Decide the handbook rules its queries implement (today KB-CPP-046). TD3: no other tool checks these rules. TCL3 Validation of the tool (suite); review of every query cppcheck (Ubuntu 24.04 archive) Partial findings for guidelines the matrix maps to cppcheck message ids. It never decides a guideline. TD1: every guideline it touches keeps review or another tool. TCL1 None needed; ru-cpp-analysis self-tests on known-bad fixtures Handbook checks ( tools/handbook_check ) Decide the forbidden-pattern rules the matrix names (exceptions, RTTI). TD1: the compilers make the same constructs hard errors. TCL1 Unit tests in the self-CI ru-misra scripts ( tools/misra/*.py ) Install the pinned tools, apply the deviation records, merge results and apply the policy. A defect could hide findings. TD2: the canary, the extraction checks, the fixture self-test and the unit tests catch silent failure. TCL2 Unit tests ( test_misra.py ), the fixture self-test with exact counts, run-time assurance in every scan A TCL2 or TCL3 tool decides a guideline only for the requirements that pass. A requirement recorded as an anomaly does not decide anything. That aspect of the guideline keeps review, or the tool named in the anomaly's disposition. Operating environment ¶ The validated configuration is exactly what tools/misra/toolchain.json pins: Item Version Integrity CodeQL bundle (CLI and standard library) 2.21.4, the CLI the pack's release supports SHA-256 of codeql-bundle-linux64.tar.zst codeql/misra-cpp-coding-standards 2.62.0 SHA-256 of the release archive and of the pack inside it Deviation script process_coding_standards_config.py tag v2.62.0, commit 6ac4b1d SHA-256 clang-tidy 20.1.0 (LLVM's PyPI wheel) pip --require-hashes PyYAML 6.0.3 pip --require-hashes Arm GNU toolchain 14.3.rel1 SHA-256 Arm publishes GCC 14, Clang 18, GCC 13 ( g++ , the CodeQL build compiler), cppcheck Ubuntu 24.04 archive (signed) Exact versions recorded at every run Runner ubuntu-24.04 Recorded in the validation report The compile flags of the validated configuration are the org warning set: -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wundef -Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . The Cortex-M configuration adds -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 . Analysing compiled code ¶ CodeQL's C/C++ extractor builds its database from the compiler invocations it traces. build-mode: none exists for C/C++, as a preview from June 2025 and generally available since October 2025 in CLI 2.23.3. It infers the translation units and flags from the files instead. GitHub's documentation says this may give less accurate results, especially with macros or defines that are not in headers. The pack's user manual requires a clean, full build of the code. Both sources: build options for compiled languages and the pack's user manual . Decision. Only traced builds. ru-misra and the suite analyse traced builds only, from a fresh build directory, with the real compiler command lines CMake writes to compile_commands.json . Build-mode none is not used. Two configurations. The preprocessor takes different paths per target, so every configuration the drivers ship is a separate database: host ( g++ ); cortex-m : the Arm GNU toolchain with the cortex-m4f flags of ru-cross-build . ESP-IDF not yet. An ESP-IDF (Xtensa) configuration is not analysed yet; see the limitations . Same compile databases for the other tools. clang-tidy and cppcheck run on the same compile databases as the CodeQL scan. Run-time checks. The extraction checks prove at every run that each translation unit of the build, and each source file under the analysed paths, is in the database. Requirements ¶ Each claim "tool T decides guideline G with rule id R" is a requirement with a stable id TV-<TOOL>-<GUIDELINE>-<NN> , for example TV-CQL-RULE-8-2-5-01 : Source of the claim Requirements The matrix's non-partial compiler entries One per compiler ( GCC , CLANG ) and diagnostic; the GCC claim also for the cross GCC ( GCCARM ) The matrix's non-partial clang-tidy entries One per check ( TIDY ) The pack's default suite One per query of each applicable guideline ( CQL ), 221 queries for 175 guidelines, minus the not-applicable guidelines The own profile pack One per query ( CQL , guideline KB-CPP-NNN ) validate.py record derives the requirements from the matrix at the pinned handbook commit, from the pack's supported list ( tests/misra-validation/codeql-supported.json , read from the pinned pack's query metadata) and from the profile pack. A new matrix claim is a new requirement, and it fails until a test proves it. Test cases ¶ A test case is a directory under tests/misra-validation/cases/ (or codeql/<pack>/validation/ ) with: Seeded violations ( bad* ): true positives, including the edge cases the guideline targets. Each seeded violation ends its line with // seeded , and every claimed tool must report on that line: a file that seeds three forms proves three detections, not one. // seeded: codeql (or another list of tools) limits a marker to the tools that report the form on that line. A bad file without a marker is a malformed case. Compliant code ( ok* ): true negatives, including near misses that must not be flagged. Every compliant file must build without a warning with the org flags on GCC and Clang. For the Cortex-M target it must also build with the cross GCC. The exact rule id in case.yml . That is the warning option, or the clang-tidy check name, or the CodeQL query id. A query's result must also carry the guideline's tag ( external/misra/id/rule-x-y-z ). The snippets are our own. None is copied from the MISRA documents, whose text and examples are licensed. Each case was reviewed against the guideline by a reviewer who did not write it (bad files violate in every seeded form, ok files comply, near misses sit at the boundary); the review findings were fixed before the suite's first release. A CodeQL query is shown on two databases per target, one of all seeded violations and one of all compliant files. Each is built by a traced compile of each file. Both are analysed with the full default suites, so every result of every query on compliant code is seen. A result of another query on a compliant file must be listed in the case's other_findings with a reason. A false positive of the pack is recorded there as misfire: ... and in the anomaly log. The suite runs on every pull request and every push to main (the self-CI, ci-misra.yml ). It runs locally with tests/misra-validation/validate.py local . Acceptance criteria ¶ Status Meaning Accepted when pass On every target of every case of the requirement, the tool reports the rule id on every marked line of every seeded file and nothing on every compliant file, except recorded false positives (listed with the requirement) Always anomaly A recorded false negative of the rule id in any case (or only recorded anomalies), with a log entry and a disposition. The rule id is then partial for the guideline Only for pack and profile queries; the guideline keeps the mitigation the disposition names fail A test does not hold, or did not run on a target Never no test No case for the requirement Never The self-CI fails ( record --check ) when any of these holds: a matrix claim (compiler, clang-tidy) is not pass ; a pack or profile query is fail or no test ; a compliant file draws an unreviewed result; the anomaly log and the cases disagree; the committed record does not match the run. Records ¶ Record Where Content Validation record tests/misra-validation/validation-record.json , committed Hashes of the toolchain, suite and matrix; exact tool versions; every requirement with its tests, runs and status Traceability traceability.md , committed Requirement → tests → result; guideline → tools of the matrix, with what is validated Validation report validation-report.md , artifact tool-validation of every self-CI run, attached to each ci-tools release Tool versions and hashes, results by tool, open problems, anomalies with dispositions, limitations, every test result Anomaly log tests/misra-validation/anomalies.yml Every known false negative and false positive, how it was found, its disposition The report is the record an auditor reads. The release attaches the report of the self-CI run that released it. Re-validation ¶ A change to any of these changes a validated tool or its configuration: toolchain.json the runner's compiler versions the compile flags a clang-tidy option a case a profile query validate.py the pinned handbook commit (the matrix) Each of these changes the record: its hashes, its versions or its results. The record check then fails the self-CI until the validation has run again and the regenerated record and traceability are committed from that run's tool-validation artifact. A version bump therefore cannot merge without its validation evidence. An update of the runner image that changes a compiler fails the self-CI the same way. Run-time assurance ¶ Validation shows the tools work. Run-time assurance shows they worked on this scan: Canary. A file with known violations ( tools/misra/canary/ru_misra_canary.cpp ) is compiled into every database. If any of its expected query results is missing, the scan fails. Extraction coverage. Every translation unit of compile_commands.json must be in the database. So must every source file under the analysed paths, through some translation unit. An extractor error (severity 4 or 5) fails the scan. Flags. Each translation unit is checked for the org flags. At the safety level, a missing flag fails, because the compiler-decided guidelines would not be enforced. Suppressions. Every marker must cite a record and deviate a finding of that record's guideline. What the tests cannot prove ¶ The review checklist covers what remains: Absence of violations of an undecidable guideline. Passing tests show detection of the seeded forms, not completeness. System-scope guidelines across a whole program, beyond the translation units of the analysed build. Code paths no analysed configuration compiles, today ESP-IDF (Xtensa). The guidelines no tool covers (Dir 0.3.2, and the review-only parts of others). Licence of CodeQL ¶ The CodeQL CLI is licensed per user, and only for these purposes: academic research; demonstrating the software; testing OSI-licensed queries; analysis of an Open Source Codebase : a codebase released under an OSI-approved licence; for an Open Source Codebase hosted on GitHub.com, creating databases in automated analysis, CI or CD. The License Restrictions exclude "any codebase that is not an Open Source Codebase". Their own example of such a codebase is a private repository. Those restrictions do not apply under a paid GitHub Advanced Security licence ( terms ). This repository is public and MIT, so the suite runs here and locally. A private driver may not be analysed, in CI or locally, until it is public under its OSI licence, or the organisation buys the licence. ru-misra enforces this before it downloads anything. That is the warning option, or the clang-tidy check name, or the CodeQL query id. A query's result must also carry the guideline's tag ( external/misra/id/rule-x-y-z ). The snippets are our own. None is copied from the MISRA documents, whose text and examples are licensed. Each case was reviewed against the guideline by a reviewer who did not write it (bad files violate in every seeded form, ok files comply, near misses sit at the boundary); the review findings were fixed before the suite's first release. A CodeQL query is shown on two databases per target, one of all seeded violations and one of all compliant files. Each is built by a traced compile of each file. Both are analysed with the full default suites, so every result of every query on compliant code is seen. A result of another query on a compliant file must be listed in the case's other_findings with a reason. A false positive of the pack is recorded there as misfire: ... and in the anomaly log. The suite runs on every pull request and every push to main (the self-CI, ci-misra.yml ). It runs locally with tests/misra-validation/validate.py local .
